name: Legends of Hermes

neighbours.name: The Vestige of Study
neighbours.summary: Conciatta's sanctum, rich and thriving, stopped in the middle of a talk: Currito leans forward in a great chair, hands shaping something in the air, and she stands at her work table with a finger on a line of an open book. Shelves of texts and devices line the walls. The window shows Moorish Saraqusta and the Noor Mosque, like a painting hung a few feet beyond the frame, and only from where she stands.
neighbours.secrets:
The open book is the journal of an unnamed magus thrown by accident into a regio that stifled his magic, who broke out by spending all his vis; the line under her finger says all of it was Vim vis. A tractatus on Vim in archaic Hermetic Latin lies beside it, arguing that the realms could only be touched by new Arts, which any magus now sees is absurd. The pages cannot be turned. The door is the way in and out.

A tempus of the Magic Realm (LoH pp. 19-21), found during a story of that realm. Those within gain the Personality Trait Studious +3 while they stay, unless they have a supernatural ability of the Magic Realm (Realms of Power: Magic p. 15). With the Magical Travel rules (same book p. 23) it has a level of 5, Ease Factor 15 to reach the next tempus. No vestige connects to the mundane world, so none leads straight to the sanctum.

neighbours.name: The Vestige of Acclaim
neighbours.summary: A great lecture hall of Durenmar, which a Bonisagus knows at once. Benches of magi of several Houses face a dais where Conciatta stands at a lectern. The scene jumps as the visitor walks the central aisle: questions, doubt and approval, arguments breaking out, and at last applause, as a few elders stalk out. Through all of it Currito sits at the back, quietly proud, and does not rise.
neighbours.secrets:
The last image, seen only from where she stands, shows the first sign of what was to come: the silver stylus on her lectern has curled in on itself and floats above the wood. The door at the rear is the way in and out.

A tempus of the Magic Realm (LoH pp. 19-21), found during a story of that realm. Those within gain the Personality Trait Proud +3 while they stay, unless they have a supernatural ability of the Magic Realm (Realms of Power: Magic p. 15). With the Magical Travel rules (same book p. 23) it has a level of 5, Ease Factor 15 to reach the next tempus. No vestige connects to the mundane world, so none leads straight to the sanctum.

neighbours.name: The Vestige of Seclusion
neighbours.summary: The foot of a winding stair that stands alone in blank whiteness, with no tower around it. Currito waits on the steps, bowed, dressed for the road with a heavy bag on his shoulder. The steps behind the visitors dissolve into mist, and those ahead end at Conciatta's door.
neighbours.secrets:
To step off the stair is to fall into the void. Behind the door there is nothing but its other side; through the keyhole is her darkened sanctum, with things floating about her as she stands weeping at her table, fists clenched. Opening the door is the way out.

A tempus of the Magic Realm (LoH pp. 19-21), found during a story of that realm. Those within gain the Personality Trait Bitter +3 while they stay, unless they have a supernatural ability of the Magic Realm (Realms of Power: Magic p. 15). With the Magical Travel rules (same book p. 23) it has a level of 5, Ease Factor 15 to reach the next tempus. No vestige connects to the mundane world, so none leads straight to the sanctum.

neighbours.name: The Vestige of Death
neighbours.summary: The foot of a bed in the convent near Toledo, where the aged Conciatta is dying. One nun holds her hand and prays, one bends to catch her words, and a senior sister stands by. Small things rise as if lifted, weakly, and fall. At her last breath the candles die, and in the gloom four figures stand in the room's four corners. Then it all begins again.
neighbours.secrets:
Her last words beg that her broken soul be gathered: one part is here, one in fire and damnation, one deep in the lost city, one at home at last. Currito's triptych of Saint Ildefonso hangs here and also exists in the mundane convent, his gift for their help with her studies (Intelligence + Church Lore simple roll against 6 names the saint). Looked at closely, it also shows the other three tempora, and is the way to each.

A tempus of the Magic Realm (LoH pp. 19-21), found during a story of that realm. Those within gain the Personality Trait Fearful +3 while they stay, unless they have a supernatural ability of the Magic Realm (Realms of Power: Magic p. 15). With the Magical Travel rules (same book p. 23) it has a level of 5, Ease Factor 15 to reach the next tempus. No vestige connects to the mundane world, so none leads straight to the sanctum.

neighbours.name: Zaragoza
neighbours.summary:
A strong walled city at the heart of Aragon, and its capital since Alfonso el Batallador took it in 1118. Good roads run north to Jaca and the river runs southeast toward Barcelona. The Ebro bounds it on the north and its tributary the Huerva on the east, with many bridges. Church spires and old minarets crowd toward the middle, and in the narrow market streets Christian, Jew and Muslim haggle side by side between the bells and the calls to prayer.

The valley rises slowly to mountains and holds desert, deep woods, plains and farms. Wheat is exported, and wine from up the Ebro makes the city rich. Spring is wet and summer a scorching drought. In winter two great cold spirits fight over the city: a fog that settles on it and a dry wind off the mountains that tries to drive the fog away.

As Saraqusta it was an Arab city of the Emirate of Cordoba in Conciatta's day, later a Taifa kingdom under the Banu Tujib and the Banu Hud, whose armies El Cid led from 1081 to 1086. The Almoravids held it from 1110.
neighbours.secrets: When Alfonso took the city many libraries went south with fleeing Muslims, and the rest were sent to Paris, where they remain in the university's care. Hermetic texts were among them, Conciatta's too (p. 22).

neighbours.name: La Torre no Vista
neighbours.summary:
In the northwest of the city, where the Ebro bends sharply back on itself, stand the home and great warehouse of the merchant Reyes de Barbastro, looking over the river. Beneath the warehouse is a low, gloomy cellar full of forgotten crates and barrels, with two pillars in its middle opposite the stairs. Its walls are plastered and whitewashed, and grubby with age. Here and there the plaster has flaked away from an older painting underneath.

It keeps the name of the covenant Currito and Conciatta founded, which is all that most know of it: birds appear and vanish in the air above the place.

levels.name: The tower
levels.see: Spells or abilities that see through regio boundaries show a stair winding around the outside of the cellar and up out of sight.
levels.enter: Taking the stair pushes a character through the boundary. From within the Dominion, Perception + Second Sight simple roll against 21, and the aura penalizes any non-Divine power used; once the ritual has made the Magic aura apparent, against 15 (p. 25). Regio rules: ArM5 p. 189.
levels.notes:
A tower of several stories, each with room for several chambers and a laboratory, and little sign of any staff. From a balcony midway up, the Aljaferia can be seen as through a mist.

Secrets
Currito's sanctum, midway up: the warped door gives way to a burst of three dozen startled birds. Centuries of guano have ruined all within; the cabinets are empty and what equipment he left lies smashed.

Conciatta's sanctum, near the top: the sanctum marker is still on the unlocked door. Perception + Awareness against 6 hears movement within. The Magical Conciatta is inside. Most of the books and devices are copies of the same few things, scraped or broken down so she could write or build them again. What is of use (pp. 26-27), each a source of insight; where noted, a lab text or device gives a bonus to the insight roll equal to its magnitude (Ancient Magic p. 8), counting only a device's highest-level effect:

Subsume the Apparent Dominion, lab text, ReVi 50 Ritual: R Touch, D Year, T Room; suppresses an apparent Dominion of strength 3 or less, and the strongest other aura present manifests. It creates a preternatural tether of level one and a +1 yearly aura modifier (Realms of Power: Magic p. 10). Conciatta's code must be broken first (ArM5 p. 102), at least a season's work. Re-creating it gives 10 points toward Confluence of the Realms.

The Sands of Time, InVi 19: a three-chambered hourglass a foot tall that shows whether a Magic aura waxes (sand runs up), wanes (runs down) or holds (gathers in the middle). R Touch, D Sun, T Ind, 2/day triggered at sunrise and sunset. Only a broken one remains, its glass smashed and sand gone; the wooden frame survives for a skilled Verditius to reforge. Broken it gives no bonus but 4 points toward Insight of the Realms; working, +3 to an insight roll.

The Lodestone, InVi 33: a palm-sized silver device with a pointer under a lens, which in a Magic aura points to the nearest tether, and wanders if the aura is diffuse. R Touch, D Sun, T Ind, 2/day triggered at sunrise and sunset. No insight bonus; re-creating the effect gives 7 points toward Insight of the Realms.

The Tome of Binro: 60 correspondences (Covenants p. 90), many in the hand of Binro, an early Bonisagus follower called a heretic half in jest for holding the founder's theory flawed. Studied as a level 6 tractatus on Magic Theory, it reveals a casting tablet of Ward Against Woodland Spirits, ReHe(Vi) 41 (R Touch, D Ring, T Circle), with penetration built in; re-created without that at level 30, it gives 9 points toward True Understanding of the Realms.

neighbours.secrets:
The cellar lies in a level 2 Dominion that subsumes a Magic aura of level 1 (p. 24). The covenant is in the regio above, which hangs high in the air. Currito raised the tower inside it by ritual after buying the land, and built wharfs and the warehouse in the mundane world as cover and income. It dissolved in 990.

Finding it (p. 23). Mercere records at Harco place it only in Saraqusta. Yuval's, the Mercer house in Barcelona (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 82), names Currito and Conciatta, says the tower rose from a regio on the south bank of the Ebro, gives a place for Redcaps in the east of the city apart from the sancta, and hints the regio lay north of the Noor Mosque. That mosque is gone: Intelligence + Zaragoza Lore against 9 shows the Aljaferia palace stands on its site. Or watch the air for birds appearing or vanishing: Perception + Awareness simple roll against 9, a week's search plus a week per point missed.

The fresco (pp. 24-25). The older painting, by Currito, is a casting tablet for Conciatta's ritual Subsume the Apparent Dominion (printed ReVi 40 here, ReVi 50 on p. 26, whose working adds to 50; 50 is followed), its Hermetic words wound among scenes of the Cordoban city. It is damaged and deliberately incomplete; the rest is the wall behind Conciatta in the illumination in Currito's journal, which shows her between these two pillars. It is the only casting tablet for the spell. With both, Intelligence + Magic Theory stress roll against 9, +1 per magus collaborating after the first, one day plus a day per point missed. On a botch the magus thinks he has it, but the casting total is 0 and he rolls six extra botch dice. Casting tablets: Covenants p. 89. Once the Dominion is subsumed the level 1 Magic aura shows and the regio is far easier to enter. Reyes knows nothing of the design.

After the reunion (p. 45). The tower gains a preternatural tether of Strength 1 and its aura aligns to Vim; 12 pawns of Vim vis lie there as crystal shards, and 4 pawns of Vim manifest in the tower on each anniversary. But the regio has lost the great being that helped tether its aura, and unless the tower returns to magical use the aura weakens over time.

neighbours.name: Toledo
neighbours.summary:
A walled city on a rocky height, the Tagus around three sides and only the north open to the land. Drab and brown from afar, within it dazzles with slender winding streets and fine squares. Near the middle of the peninsula, it draws people from all Iberia. It is the heart of the Iberian church, and was so even under Islam. Christians, Jews and Muslims all practice freely, the Jews better treated than in most Christian cities, and for a century a school of translation has brought in texts from across the known world, so a scholar may find nearly anything.

Castles of the military orders ring the city, and two orders are open rivals here. The Order of Calatrava, Benedictine, wears a red cross fleurdelisée on white, and only lately won back its name after losing its castle to the Almohades; it suspects its rivals of corruption. The Knights of Santiago, Augustinian, wear a red cross ending in a sword, protect pilgrims, and admit secular knights and lay members; they think the Calatravans weak.
neighbours.secrets: Dominion aura 4 by day (p. 28).

neighbours.name: Convento de San Ildefonso
neighbours.summary:
Low whitewashed buildings behind a low, dusty white wall, off the road a short way from Toledo, with a few dry fields behind and almond trees bleached of color by the sun. Inside, the convent sinks into the ground around a sunken courtyard with narrow tiled cloisters. It is poor and lives on Toledo's charity. A young novice here is said to receive divine visions, and the wealthy of Toledo and beyond sometimes come to consult her. Abbess Prudencia does not admit men inside the wall unless she trusts them or they are plainly very rich.

The small graveyard lies some way off in the shade of a low hill. One small headstone bears the name of Conciatta.
neighbours.secrets:
The aura is a constant level 5 (p. 28). By custom, the novice who last carried Conciatta's spirit lies in that grave when she dies; Conciatta's bones, like those of every later host, were moved to the ossuary, and no record says which are hers.

The audience (pp. 29-30). No outsider may see the holy sister, but money buys a seeming audience the next day: one visitor, with Prudencia and an attendant, addresses a curtain. Behind it her other attendant plays the seer, telling of a long journey, revelations, slights borne by grace, and acting both forcefully and temperately. If the sham is exposed Prudencia does not apologize, and shows them the girl, thinking that will send them away.

Automatic Writing (p. 30): a great heap of scrolls, books and slates written by the hosts out of Conciatta's knowledge. A season's collating yields several tractatus, of the storyguide's making, on Magic Theory, Vim and Dominion Lore, and a lab text for a large casting circle enchanted with Maintaining the Unstable Conjuration, ReVi 30, Pen +16, 3/day (R Personal, D Ring, T Circle): it sustains a spell of level 15 or less cast within, even the non-Hermetic magic of the Learned Magicians, until the target leaves or another spell is cast there. Built, it is a large iron ring in pieces, riveted in brass to the floor and opened with 20 pawns of vis; it gives a +1 specialization in experimentation and +1 Safety. The text gives +6 to the insight roll, and finishing the ring gives 6 points toward Confluence of the Realms. The notes call this one of four effects for one Greater Enchanted Device, the others for the other realms and for spirits' non-Hermetic effects, which implies Infernal spirits once aided her.

neighbours.name: Qadis
neighbours.summary:
An ancient city still in Moorish hands, on a sand spit in the Atlantic a little northwest of the Pillars of Hercules. Its loose ground bears few tall buildings, so the skyline sits low, but the port is busy, its view full of masts from all the world. The mouth of the Guadalquivir is a day's ride north.

Old Qadis does not lie quiet. At sunset the living give the city over to its dead, a thousand ghosts or more from all its long history, who go about their affairs unseen by most. Strangers, and magi above all, draw their interest.
neighbours.secrets: Dominion aura 2 on average, 1 at night, and the city is full of lacunae of Magic, Faerie and Infernal (p. 33). After some days, Second Sight or fit magic shows ghosts watching the characters: loose-formed specters sent by stronger masters, who mostly flee if challenged. Then the characters begin to see others abroad at night. The storyguide may offer a ghost ally, who can make introductions and point out places of power, and will expect something in return.

neighbours.name: The Roman Theater of Qadis
neighbours.summary: A sunken half-circle of chipped and broken marble steps, disused for centuries and stripped of all else. Stories of its haunting are likely why it was never built over. The living know the place, but not the name of the actor who holds it; the dead know both, and come often to watch.
neighbours.secrets: Seiffeddin is its only ghost. The dead attend less for love of his art than from the constraints of their own roles (p. 34).

neighbours.name: The Guadalquivir Marshes
neighbours.summary: The marshes around the Guadalquivir delta, a day's ride north of Qadis. Bits of an ancient wall lie out in them, and a witch's torch moves about by night.
neighbours.secrets: Other faeries here lure the unwary to their doom (Realms of Power: Faerie p. 92). Faerie aura 2 where the city stood; sections of the old walls lie in Faerie regiones (same book p. 16).

neighbours.name: Tartessos
neighbours.summary:
Once a mighty trading city, silver-rich, whose metal paid for Greece's defense against the Persians, which traded with the Tin Islands and the Phoenicians under its absolute king Arganthonios. A great calamity sank it into the sea in a single day. It lives now only in the Faerie Realm.

Lightning flashes in a sky of rolling thunder over endless ruins, and the weeping of an unseen dying people comes from all around. Every brick that falls has another about to fall. At the center stands the shell of a palace, all pillars and broken arches.

levels.name: The city gates
levels.see: Two broken pillars and great shards of rotted wood rise from the marsh.
levels.enter: Only on the anniversary of the city's loss, one night a year; a guide is needed to find it and to cross the Threshold into the Faerie Realm (p. 35).
levels.notes:
A faerie regio of the old walls and the way into the city.

Secrets
If using Realms of Power: Faerie (p. 20): Threshold Strength 24; on the anniversary the Threshold Total is already 15 (6 for the gates, 9 for the night), before personal Thresholds, artistic endeavor and Arcadian Mysteries. Bruja's potion can add the rest. Without that book, Bruja is simply able to guide them through, and frogs are still involved. Bruja, as guardian of the road, then offers a choice of kingdoms of silver and gold or a kingdom of loss and despair: Tartessos is the kingdom of loss, and any other answer makes the road vanish and sends them back to Qadis (p. 36).

neighbours.secrets:
The story's theme is reunification (pp. 36-37). Each challenge passed leads closer to the palace; each failure closer to the mundane world. Examples: a mother crying for her lost daughter; two brothers fighting over the last loaf; a statue of a young warrior who has lost his spear, which lies in the path (Excellent quality long spear, +2 attack and defense): return it and he points the way, take it and robbers may come; an old man whose well bucket has fallen, who leads to the palace only if the well is mended. Two or more passed find the palace; three failed find a facade whose doors lead out to the mundane world. Each success earns a Fable Point (Realms of Power: Faerie p. 21).

Bruja brings the characters to the road but does not go in; she meets them when they leave, gives them a book with a warning not to open it until the other side, and summons the Threshold. The book holds the Faerie Conciatta.

neighbours.name: Narixa
neighbours.summary: A small, wealthy Muslim town on the Mediterranean shore of Al Andalus, with white beaches below, low mountains behind that fall to fine cliffs, and silks famous across the Muslim world. Fishing boats launch daily from the sand, and the markets are full of fish, livestock, fruit and grain; the merchant quarter trades silk, spice and European goods among street players and the calls to prayer. There are few dhimmis this far into Al Andalus, but people from all the Islamic world. The poor quarters mistrust foreigners, the rich ones are used to them, and men who look for trouble find it.
neighbours.secrets: Dominion aura 3 over most of its lands (p. 40). The town knows little of the evil in the mountains.

neighbours.name: The Al Narixa Mosque
neighbours.summary: A mosque with a long-tended library, among the many that fill Narixa's skyline. Its imams have little interest in helping foreigners hunt old scrolls, but may send the persuasive to Hamid ibn Harun, who keeps the library.
neighbours.secrets:
Conciatta and Currito left many notes here on the last of their visits, well over two centuries ago (p. 40).

Conciatta's Scrolls (p. 41): collated, a map of a cave system two miles east of the town, with how to find and enter it, and a warning of tunnels where the unwary slip between regio levels unawares. It gives +1 to rolls to navigate the caves and their regiones.

The Insightful Stylus (p. 41): in a small sealed leather case marked Conciatta ex Bonisagus, a slender silver stylus traced with Hermetic and occult symbols of the Infernal, and a scrap of parchment on its effects. Opened with 12 pawns of vis. Sense the Line, InVi 14, Pen +0, constant (R Touch, D Sun, T Ind): detects the line of an Infernal regio boundary. Inscribe the Line, ReTe 14, Pen +0, constant (R Personal, D Sun, T Ind): held to a wax tablet, the stylus traces that boundary in miniature, at the speed of a magus drawing a circle. Note These Landmarks, ReTe 14, Pen +0, unlimited (R Personal, D Mom, T Ind): at a Latin command it marks distances and landmarks, even while inscribing. It must be investigated in the laboratory, and is then a source of insight; re-creating it gives 5 points toward Insight of the Realms.

neighbours.name: The Narixa Caves
neighbours.summary: Ancient caves in the low mountains two miles east of Narixa, of deep fissures and domed chambers. Mice, scorpions and snakes swarm over floor and wall, and the laughter of hyena echoes from somewhere deep inside. Here and there human bones jut from the rock.

levels.name: The throne room
levels.see: A huge domed chamber, its floor split by chasms, flames running on the walls, and at its far end craggy steps that sweep out over a wide fiery chasm to a throne of writhing serpents.
levels.notes:
A level 5 Tartaran regio, and the heat is unbearable.

Secrets
The fight should be deadly (p. 44). The storyguide sets the numbers; all the beasts mean to kill. A hyena pack that holds a positive grapple strength two rounds running drags its enemy to a chasm: Dexterity + Athletics or Climb stress against 9 to cling on. If he fails, another who has not acted may fast-cast, or leap to catch him (Quickness + Athletics stress against 9): both end prone and must recover their weapons. Climbing back is Dexterity + Climb stress against 9. A fall ends in the lava hundreds of feet below.

neighbours.secrets:
A hive of corrupted beasts, jinn and demons. A level 3 Malevolent Infernal aura, with Tartaran regiones throughout (Realms of Power: The Infernal pp. 15-16). Unlike most, these regiones bleed into each other as the tunnels do, and the bones are those of victims caught between a regio and the mundane world. The unprepared are certain to be lost for good (pp. 39-41).

All terrain is hazardous: an extra botch die on physical actions, and large weapons at -2 to attack and defense. Three events should test the party on the way to the throne room (pp. 41-43). A sheer face: three climb rolls of rising difficulty (6, 9, 12, say); a failure starts a fall with an initiative of 6, for fast-casting; a botch may be lethal or draw him into a regio, and Area Lore: Narixa Caves stress against 12 finds him. A rock fall: those beating an initiative of 6 may react, and the rest are as in a collapsing stone building (ArM5 p. 181). Hyena ambush: Perception + Awareness against their stealth; a pack splits, two dragging one victim toward a regio and three blocking the rest. After four rounds he is taken deeper: a grog is dead, any other may fight free and flee the regio.

neighbours.name: The Ghosts of Qadis
neighbours.summary: The dead of Qadis, perhaps a thousand or more, who have accepted that they persist and get on with their affairs by night. They split into factions by nation, former calling and era.

details.decides: By how well each recalls mortal life; lucid apparitions rule and use mindless specters as tools.
details.wants: To protect their interests, descendants and city; few care to be laid to rest.

neighbours.secrets:
The ranks follow the ghost types of Realms of Power: Magic p. 115, with apparitions at the top (p. 35).

Faeries, drawn here for centuries, now fill the roles of the recently dead, who mostly get proper burial and do not linger. They think themselves ghosts, differ only in their Might, and feed on the living by quietly touching their lives. Demons take the forms of the dead too, to corrupt the living, and the Magic and Faerie ghosts fight them as best they can.

neighbours.name: The Four Corners of the World
neighbours.summary: Conciatta's spirit is sundered, with an aspect in each of four auras or regiones across Iberia: her sanctum, the convent of her last years, the sunken faerie city of Tartessos, and the depths of the Narixa caves. Whoever finds them may gather her treasures and make her whole.

stages.title: History Unfolding
stages.clues: During a story of the Magic Realm the magi find tempora of her life: pick the one that fits and let the players explore. They give her past, hints of her discoveries and fate, and where her sanctum was.

stages.title: Currito's Journal
stages.clues: A delegation brings one magus news that his pater has died or gone to Final Twilight, with a tattered heirloom in an unknown hand and word to read it well. It is Currito's book, and each delegate wants it: a Quaesitor who suspects foul play, a Bonisagus who wants its magic public, and a Redcap who offers a small fortune for Zebulon. It may instead lie in the covenant's library or in Currito's old sanctum (pp. 21-22).

stages.title: The Tower by the Water
stages.clues: The Mercere records, or watching the birds, lead to Reyes de Barbastro's warehouse in Zaragoza. See La Torre no Vista.
stages.stopped: Fresco and journal together give the ritual that opens the way to the Magical Conciatta (pp. 22-27).

stages.title: Her Final Resting Place
stages.clues: Prudencia guards the possessed novice Immaculada outside Toledo. The characters must win access, then decide how to deal with what they find; the setting asks for mercy and sacrifice. The girl's words point to Seiffeddin in Qadis.
stages.stopped: Her fear of being alone is eased, and the Divine Conciatta passes to a willing new host (pp. 27-32).

stages.title: The Lost City
stages.clues: In Qadis the dead know Seiffeddin, who sends them to Bruja on the marsh, on the one night the gates open.
stages.ignored: They fail three of the city's tests and are turned back to the mundane world.
stages.stopped: Reminded of Currito's love, the Faerie Conciatta is released and leaves in Bruja's book (pp. 32-39).

stages.title: The Descent
stages.clues: Hamid ibn Harun finds them Conciatta's scrolls; the caves lie two miles east of Narixa.
stages.stopped: The Infernal Conciatta is bound or captured, however the troupe contrives it, and carried off (pp. 39-45).

stages.title: The Return
stages.clues: In the tower wait the scholar, the Divine spirit in its host, the bound Infernal aspect, who curses them all and shocks the Magical one, and the Faerie self in its book.
stages.ignored: If any aspect is destroyed along the way, all perish at that moment.
stages.stopped: By a rite of the troupe's devising, the Faerie self steps from the book and the Divine rises from the host. Divine joins Infernal, Faerie joins Magic, and these two become one white-burning shard that pierces floor and ceiling and flashes through all present. For a moment the Magic Realm opens with scenes of her life on the walls, and then she is gone. She leaves 12 pawns of Vim vis in crystal shards (p. 45).

neighbours.secrets:
It can run as one story or as separate episodes, moving the clues to spread it out (p. 18). The history and the journal come in either order, and the four aspects in any order the troupe likes (p. 19); the numbers on this track are only the book's order of telling.

Foreshadowing (p. 19): raise her name in unrelated stories. Run stories that turn on auras, or on the lack of any way to find what anchors one. Old casting tablets on auras, books or devices Currito took, her glosses in others' works, and his frescoes may all surface; any study of Vim from a book can bring up her name.

Moving it (p. 19): Tartessos could be Sybaris in the Roman Tribunal, Zaragoza could be Paris with the Seine for the Ebro, and Jerusalem could stand for Toledo.

Rewards (p. 45): a suggested 5 experience points for the events around each aspect, 20 in all. Experience in the Magic Realm comes as vis that can transform a character (Realms of Power: Magic pp. 20, 26). Bonisagus Acclaim: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 21 and p. 45 here.

Aftermath (p. 45): magi still need a separate effect for each realm. Letting Vim spells affect every realm without re-invention would be a Hermetic Breakthrough, which her Virtues reduce to a Major Breakthrough, with troupe approval; a further Major Breakthrough can fully integrate each of hers, so that all who study the sources may use Realm Lore. Whoever brings her secrets back ties his name to hers; whoever takes them further wins fame of his own.

neighbours.name: The Invisible Enemy
neighbours.summary: A private messenger comes from a magus of a foreign Tribunal, who is said to be curious about Currito of Jerbiton's early years, and offers a good price for the journal. It seems odd that the master will not settle for a chance to study it: he wants the book itself.
neighbours.secrets: The messenger unknowingly carries possessing spirits across the Aegis (Realms of Power: The Infernal p. 32). Inside, they hunt for the book and spread fear and mischief (p. 21).

neighbours.name: The Generous Knight of Santiago
neighbours.summary: A knight of Santiago befriended on the road invites the characters to his castle for his birthday, and his wife has brought food, wine and players from all Iberia. His dour priest scorns the excess and refuses the feast.

details.antagonist: The debauched Infernal aura of a knight's feast

neighbours.secrets: The priest may be right. How long until the magi notice the debauched Infernal aura? Will they give in? And must they either let the devil win or damage the knight's name (p. 28)?

neighbours.name: The Books of Al-Mu'taman
neighbours.summary: Yusuf ibn Ahmad al-Mu'taman ibn Hud ruled Zaragoza from 1082 to 1085 and wrote at length on geometry. Readers of his works find references to magic there too.

details.antagonist: None; a lineage to find and bargain with

neighbours.secrets: He was a Learned Magician (Hedge Magic Revised Edition p. 79), of a line that taught Conciatta its ways past the ill effects of auras. Modern magi might learn much from them, if they can be found and bargained with (p. 23).

neighbours.name: The Spirit-Binders of Qadis
neighbours.summary: Workers of spirit magic come to Qadis from time to time in search of strong new servants. Those allowed to leave go away disappointed.
neighbours.secrets: The ghosts will not stand for any attempt to control them, and unite against whoever tries (p. 35).

neighbours.name: Fortunata's Island
neighbours.summary:
A small, low island, a mile or two across, no different from a distance from the countless others of the Mediterranean. If it has a name, only the fishermen nearby know it, and they keep away for the foul weather.

Sandy beaches, dunes and dune grass ring it, and the storms leave driftwood along the shore. The ground rises 100 to 200 feet at the centre, where gorse, thorn and olive take over. Springs in the interior feed streams that run through gullies in the dunes to the sea, with mussels and small fish in them, crabs in the creeks, and sea fish for anyone who dares the weather.

The beaches are featureless, and walkers lose count of the distance and cannot tell whose tracks they are following. Voices and music drift about the interior; people and buildings show in the distance, even a village, and are gone at the next turn. The ghosts of drowned sailors sometimes march along the shore. From a few places a Roman villa can be seen, before the dunes hide it again.
neighbours.secrets:
Location: the book leaves it open, with the governing Tribunal, for each saga to choose (pp. 56, 59). It offers the Tyrrhenian, the Adriatic, the Ionian, the Aegean or even the Balearics. Its text uses the Ionian Sea as its stand-in, which would put the island off the west coast of Greece between the Roman and Theban Tribunals, and wherever it says Ionian Lore it means the Area Lore of the saga's choice.

Finding it by study (p. 56): after a season with her personal writings, roll Intelligence + Mediterranean Lore against Ease Factor 18, or Intelligence + Ionian Islands Lore against 15. Success gives a hunch where to look. A botch gives a false trail, which a visit clears up, and later study may still give the true place. Her writings describe how she lived, not where, so they are poor geography.

Vis (p. 60): magi who take the time to study the island can find sources of about 20 pawns a year, of Rego, Muto, Aquam, Auram, Imaginem, Mentem and Vim. The book gives neither the sources nor the split.

Bound spirits (p. 59): Fortunata cast a command spell on each guardian and made it permanent by Spell Binding, each in a container now in the laboratory. Whoever holds a container may claim to rule that spirit. Breaking one ends the Sustain spell and the command, and frees both spirits. A spell that countermands an active command must exceed its level and penetrate the spirit's Magic Resistance, so finding and breaking the container is usually easier.

Tempestas's binding is the book's example: Coerce a Spirit of Auram (ReAu 15, Touch, Diameter, Individual; base 5, +1 Touch, +1 Diameter), held by Sustain a Spell of Auram (ReVi(Au) 20, Touch, Special, Individual, Ritual; four pawns of vis) and a lesser Auram spirit. Cheaper than an invested constant effect, it uses her own cast-spell Penetration. The book gives that lesser spirit Might 20 in one place and Might 15 in another (p. 59).

Countermanding it means beating level 15 and Tempestas's Might 35, or level 20 and the lesser spirit's Might.

The spirits often lack the Might to pass even a shared Parma Magica, but they work indirectly on magi and are very dangerous to companions and grogs parted from them by the storm. They are also part of the treasure, for whoever finds their containers (p. 67).

neighbours.name: Fortunata's Villa
neighbours.summary:
A house in the Roman manner, built new by a maga and not preserved from antiquity, after the Jerbiton villas of Valnastium. A central range of two stories runs about 120 feet, with two longer side ranges of stores and workrooms reaching 150 feet south. It is shaded against the summer sun and has fireplaces for winter.

It has been ill kept. The straw is old and stale, and most rooms are shuttered and damp, their furnishings under mouldering drapes and spider webs. Candle flames burn throughout, and mirrors hang on the walls. A corridor winds through the building, broken by some rooms, many of which open into one another; pillars moulded with Hermetic motifs frame the outer doors and those of the larger rooms. The best rooms, her bedchamber and dining room among them, have mosaic floors and painted walls in a classical style, now damaged.

Mirrors here do not reflect truly, shadows move by themselves, and the spiders are alarmingly large, legs nearly a hand-span across and bodies bigger than a man's thumb.
neighbours.secrets:
The high aura has warped the contents (p. 61). Magi casting Sight spells from outside soon learn they see only an image of the villa, not the house (p. 60).

Who is where (pp. 61-62): Imagines such as Error and Cantus gather here for the aura and to tease the mirrors, and treat strangers as toys. Lucida moves through the library, the laboratory and Fortunata's bedroom, scolding Monocaudus. He lurks by the kitchen fire, and spends much of the day outdoors on the excuse of firewood or food. The flames are Fax's.

Those who search only the open rooms find an abandoned house. The laboratory and library take careful looking (p. 55).

neighbours.name: The Villa Graveyard and Necromanteion
neighbours.summary:
A small graveyard beside the villa, where the dead rest in stone urns.

Beside it are a spring and a pool among cypress trees, and a false doorway in the villa's north wall, sheltered by an arch and closed by an iron gate, with mosaics of Hades within.
neighbours.secrets: Many of the urns hold pagan burials brought from elsewhere and re-interred so that their ghosts could be called with ease. The false doorway is a necromanteion, once used in ceremonies to reach the dead (p. 62). The book prints no aura for the graveyard itself, so none is entered; the island's is 4 and the villa's 6.

neighbours.name: Fortunata's Laboratory and Library
neighbours.summary: A room at the core of the house, surrounded by others, with no door and no window. The rooms around it are laid out so that its absence is not obvious.
neighbours.secrets:
Careful study or mapping shows the missing space, but only magic gets in. Monocaudus has never entered; only Lucida knows the secret (p. 62). It is surprisingly sparse, since much of her work was done outdoors among spirits. Cleaned, with its perishable stocks replaced, it would serve as a standard laboratory.

The book says four tractatus, a summa and nine Initiation Scripts, but names eight (p. 64); the ninth may be the lost Hermetic Synthemata script.

Principles Lore (pp. 47-50): an Organization Lore she devised to order the Initiations she made, which serves as Cult Lore for a set of Initiations with no cult: no ranks, no hierarchy, no fixed sequence. Some study of it is needed before any script can be used. Magi already in a Mystery Cult can adapt the texts to that cult. She practised it for whole seasons; a season's Practice of a Cult Lore has Source Quality 4, or 5 if inspired by a compatible text of another cult (p. 49).

Self-Initiation (pp. 49-50): the maga is her own Mystagogue, with her own Presence and Lore, at the Target Levels for a Virtue she lacks. Initiation is summarised on p. 50 and given in full in The Mysteries: Revised Edition, chapter 2. Adapting an existing organization needs troupe approval and a mystical character; otherwise devise a new Ability.

Adapting a script (pp. 49-51): study another cult's script for a week, then Intelligence + that cult's Lore against 9 to understand it, or study again; a botch gives a false script. Modifying a component is Intelligence + own Lore against 12, replacing an element against 15, and adding a Quest (+3 Script Bonus) against 9. Keep a record of Ordeals: they lower the next three Initiation Totals. Scripts that overlap may have spent the same Quests and Ordeals. Sacrifices repeat more easily than Ordeals.

Earlier scripts have higher bonuses, from when her Lore was low; later ones assume mastery. Partial order (p. 49): Spirit Familiar; Minor Magical Focus, with the Ordeal; Major Magical Focus, first after it; Spell Binding, second; Hermetic Empowerment, third. A script for Hermetic Synthemata (The Mysteries: Revised Edition p. 87) is gone from the library.

The Mastery of Principles, Puissant Principles Lore, +2 to the score (p. 51). Quest for lost texts on the Lore, then write a new one; Vow to resurrect the Principles (an Ordeal, Minor Flaw); second Quest, three other magi study the text and each write a tractatus in return. At dawn on midwinter solstice, on a remote magical high peak (she suggests Olympus or the Great Pyramid), burn incense and give 5 pawns to the spirits of magic. Initiation Total 18, Script Bonus 16: Ordeal 3, Quest 3, Quest 3, Place and Time 3, Initiate's Time 1, Sacrifice of Vis 1, Sympathy 2. Needs Presence + Lore 2. It seems she never used it; she left copies for others, and they sit forgotten in covenant libraries.

The Myth of Andros and the Tree, Spirit Familiar (pp. 51-52), adapted from a Greek rite of union with spirits. Quest to find and free the spirit; Quest to beat and imprison its enemy; a place and time deeply significant to the pair, for the troupe to settle. Total 18, Script Bonus 12: Quest 3, Quest 3, Place and Time 3, Sympathy 3. The Virtue is in The Mysteries: Revised Edition p. 66; here bonding level is the spirit's Might + 25, and the cords are the Hermes, Isis and Hekate Cords (p. 52).

Plutonic Beginnings, Minor Magical Focus (commanding spirits) (pp. 52-53), from a Roman cult of the dead. Suffer the torments of free spirits and command them aloud, under the vows of the Principles. The Ordeal gives the Major Flaw Necessary Condition (speak the names of spirits): she must always cast aloud, and hearers may know the invocations. She meant pagan gods; varying it to saints is an Intelligence + Principles Lore roll against 12, or the troupe may count saints as spirits. Covers Rego (Form) that commands insubstantial spirits of any Form, no Technique requisites. Total 18, Script Bonus 12: Major Ordeal 9, Sympathy 3.

The Myth of Aerius and Pluto, Major Magical Focus (spirit magic) (p. 53). Replaces any Minor Magical Focus. Defeat a spirit of Might 20 or more, then use it to defeat a second as strong. At midnight on All Hallow's Eve, at the second defeat's site, free the first and give it a rook of vis. Covers Rego (Form) on insubstantial spirits, requisites allowed, and other Techniques with a Rego requisite. Total 21 (30 less 9 for the Ordeal), Script Bonus 13: Required Virtue 3, Place and Time 3, Quest 3, Quest 3, Sacrifice 1. Needs Presence + Lore 8.

The Myth of Heiro and the Cave, Spell Binding (pp. 53-54; the Virtue is in The Mysteries: Revised Edition p. 27). She found a flawless natural bubble of glass almost too fine to see. On the first new moon after midwinter she crawled without light or magic to the heart of a deep cave system in the Alps, and forced a spirit, still without magic, into the ball to sustain a spell of light, the one spell allowed. Tales differ on the spirit: a beaten foe freed on a promise, a bribed ghost, a tricked mountain elemental. Total 12 (18 less 6, as second after the Ordeal), Script Bonus 6: Place and Time 3, Quest 3. Needs Presence + Lore 6.

The Myth of Heiro and the Haunted Graveyard, Hermetic Empowerment (pp. 54-55; the Virtue is in The Mysteries: Revised Edition p. 64). Enchant a device in a graveyard, abandoned or hidden in, building a laboratory there (Basic Laboratory, ArM5 p. 94: a season, 500 square feet, -3 to Lab Totals; Covenants chapter 9). At least 5 pawns, each from the destruction of a different ghost: one pawn of its remains goes into the device, the rest to the spirits. A lesser device will do. On a quarter-day burn the device in the graveyard on a pyre of rare woods and incense, dawn to dusk. Total 18 (15 as third after the Ordeal), Script Bonus 9: Place and Time 3, Quest 3, Sacrifice 1, Sympathy 2. Graveyards usually have Divine aura 4, fading once abandoned; church rites keep Christian dead from rising, so look to those buried outside or to ancient pagan ground.

On A Pilgrimage To Jerusalem, Sense Holiness & Unholiness, and The Myth of Aquila's Eyes, Improved Characteristics (Perception): listed on p. 64, with no other detail in the book.

Her own works on Principles Lore (p. 64):
- Principles for a Better Life, tractatus, Quality 11
- Principles of Life as a Magus, tractatus, Quality 11
- Principles of Power, tractatus, Quality 11
- Principles of the Spirit, tractatus, Quality 11
- De Disciplinae Fortunatae (Fortunata's Principles), summa, Level 4, Quality 11

Other texts (p. 64):
- Heroes of Olympos, tractatus on Magic Lore, Quality 7, Latin, by Julius of Nicomedia
- Heroes and Gods, tractatus on Magic Lore, Quality 8, Greek, by Polymos
- Necronomicus, tractatus on Necronomicus Lore, a forgotten cult, Quality 8, Latin, anonymous
- Piraeon, tractatus on Piraeon Lore, a forgotten cult, Quality 9, Greek, anonymous, with her Latin translation
- Cult of the Wanderer: revised edition, tractatus on Cult of the Wanderer Lore, a forgotten cult, Quality 9, her Latin translation of a lost anonymous Greek original
- Heroes of Rome, tractatus on Magic Lore, Quality 8, and on Mediterranean Lore (history), Quality 8, Latin, by Caius of Mediolanum
- Ionian Isles, tractatus on Mediterranean Lore, Quality 11, by Fortunata
- The Names of Ghosts, tractatus on Magic Lore, Quality 11, by Fortunata, listing the ghosts she called and what use they were, such as the tongues they read
- Ordinary Hermetic summae and tractatus on Magic Theory, Imaginem, Ignem, Terram, Mentem, Vim and all five Techniques; the book gives no titles or figures

Lab Texts (p. 65):
- Coerce the Spirit of (Form), Re(Form) 20, Voice, Diameter, Individual (base 5, +2 Voice, +1 Diameter): obeys while she can threaten it. Coerce the Spirit of Earth (Te), Coerce the Spirit of Fire (Ig), Coerce the Spirit of Illusion (Im), Coerce Ghosts (Me)
- Incantation of Summoning the Dead, ReMe 40, Arcane, Concentration, Individual, Ritual (ArM5 p. 152). Can call a ghost haunting the area if its full name is known, though a non-Ritual spell can too
- Summon the Spirit of (Form), Re(Form) 40, Arcane, Concentration, Individual (base 15, +4 Arcane, +1 Concentration): needs an Arcane Connection or the spirit's non-magical name; the element serves as a Connection to a spirit residing in the area. Summon the Spirit of Earth (Te), Summon the Spirit of Fire (Ig), Summon the Spirit of Illusion (Im), Summon the Spirit of Man (Me). The last is a lesser non-Ritual Incantation of Summoning the Dead, reaching only a ghost actively haunting something, or one the caster has already called
- Thoughts Within Babble, InMe 30, Personal, Sun, Hearing (base 5, +2 Sun, +3 Hearing): her version lasts the day, so she need not concentrate while texts are read to her
- Sustain a Spell of (Form), ReVi(Form), general, Touch, Individual, Ritual, Mystery (Spell Binding): for Terram, Ignem, Imaginem and Mentem, at levels 20, 30 and 40. Duration Special on pp. 53 and 59, Momentary on p. 65
- Empowering Prison of the Declining Spirit, Re(Mu)Vi(Form), general enchantment, Mystery (Hermetic Empowerment), Personal, Momentary, Individual, Pen +0, 1 use a day: for Terram, Ignem, Imaginem and Mentem, at levels 20, 34 and 50

Guidelines (p. 65, from The Mysteries: Revised Edition p. 28): level 5, control a disembodied spirit of (Form); level 15, summon one.

Spell Binding (p. 53): cast the Ritual on a container, then the second spell while it lasts, or in the next round if it is Momentary. The second spell must be longer than Momentary and not a Ritual. Force a spirit into the container in that time and the spell lasts until the spirit is freed by dispelling or by breaking the container. The spirit must share something with the spell, as an elemental its element, and have Might of at least the spell's level. The Ritual's base level (guideline) must at least equal that level, and requires the spell's Forms.

Hermetic Empowerment (p. 54): a device holds Ritual effects paid for by a bound spirit, each use draining the effect's magnitude from its Might Score, with effect level at most twice that score, so it is never quite emptied. Empowering Prison (guideline) has requisites for every Form it powers, base level at least twice the spirit's Might, and uses a day that limit the Ritual effects a day. The bound spirit spends Might only to resist, can use costless powers, and is freed if the Prison is disenchanted or the device broken. The draining is agony: breaking the device is likely to free a maddened spirit that feels no gratitude.

The Spell Binding containers (pp. 59-60, 65-66, 69): set into the solid stone of the floor by Rego Terram; Intellego Vim shows them. A carved agate head holds Tempestas, a large ruby Fax, a leaden plumb-weight Lapidosus. The book names these three and says the guardians include them.

Calling the Dead, ReMe 60, Pen +20, 24/day, Arcane, Concentration, Individual (p. 65): calls a ghost with a regular haunt if the user is there, or one already called by magic, given an Arcane Connection such as its full name. Suits spirits first called by Ritual. The Staff keeps up the concentration until the ghost is dismissed. (Base 15, +4 Arcane, +1 Concentration, +10 levels Penetration, +5 levels 24/day, +5 maintain concentration.)

Maintain the Caster's Spell, ReVi 45, Pen +0, 24/day, Touch, Diameter, Individual (p. 65): holds up a spell of level 40 or below that the user has cast and is concentrating on, for a Diameter, while she does other things, and she may still concentrate to alter it. (Base 30, +1 Touch, +1 Diameter, +5 levels 24/day.) Per the errata (p. 78) this effect was invested in her Talisman, relies on a Talisman's closer tie to its maker, and works for no other magus, though laboratory investigation shows it.

The book says Staff of the first effect and the errata Talisman of the second; neither says they are one object, or where it lies.

neighbours.name: Fortunata's House in Venice
neighbours.summary: An old house in Venice, sold cheaply after standing empty for a while. It was once a meeting place of Redcaps, and a rich welcome waited for them here; few now remember whose it was.
neighbours.secrets:
The book gives its street and quarter no more than the city, and no aura. It is haunted by Lucio, who has frightened off earlier owners without meaning to.

Any magus knows of a house in Venice on Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore against 6, or Intelligence + Mercere Lore against 3; a Redcap knows that this is that house against 9 (p. 56).

She hid papers behind wall panels and under floorboards. A search finds personal papers and letters, a partial catalog of her library, and letters to contacts on several small islands about small purchases and favours. Intelligence + Mediterranean Lore against 9 shows that those islands lie close together, and probably near hers.

neighbours.name: Omaion's Cave
neighbours.summary: A cave in a remote waste in Turkey.
neighbours.secrets: The home of Omaion the Serpent, in the book's main version of him (p. 58). The book says nothing more of where it lies.

neighbours.name: The Heirs of Cupressa
neighbours.summary: Witches of Algiers and the lands around, who revere the great Cupressa and have slowly spread into southern Europe, gathering what they can through paid agents.

details.wants: The treasures of Fortunata's island, which they hold were stolen from Cupressa and are rightly theirs.

neighbours.secrets: A tradition like the Witches of Thessaly (Realms of Power: The Infernal p. 140). They have met Hermetic magi before and fear the Parma Magica and strong spells, so they work through mundane agents who know nothing of their purpose or origin (p. 57). The book gives no number, leader or block.

neighbours.name: Finding Fortune
neighbours.summary:
A loose adventure played over several sessions and not in a straight line: the search for Fortunata's forgotten island, its guardians and her library (p. 55). It may open with her texts, found on a back shelf or in a treasure chest.

Any of the story starters can open it, or lead the seekers on. Some give direct evidence, some cross paths with her history without warning.

stages.title: The trail is found
stages.clues: A text, a witness or a story crossing her history tells the magi of Fortunata.

stages.title: The search
stages.clues: The island is hidden and largely forgotten. A direct search will probably fail, but others can give leads, sometimes unknowingly.

stages.title: A tempestuous approach
stages.clues: Near the island a magical storm raised by a guardian spirit breaks the vessel and casts the party ashore, scattered.

stages.title: Beset on the island
stages.clues: Strange spirits close in. The Parma Magica shields magi from direct assault, though many spirits strike indirectly, and grogs parted from their magi may be driven mad.

stages.title: The villa
stages.clues: Some reach the mansion, apparently abandoned and decayed. Only a careful search finds the library, the laboratory and the treasure in them.

neighbours.secrets: Her writings never mention the guardians, so they come as a surprise (p. 59). The treasures become a saga's own quests: the Initiations' Quests are story seeds that take the others to the far corners of Mythic Europe, in supporting or even opposing roles (pp. 47-48).

neighbours.name: In a Locked Box
neighbours.summary:
A locked metal box, marked by salt-water corrosion and tightly sealed, turns up among a treasure, in a corner of an old covenant's library, or with a merchant who could not get it open and now wants to sell it.

Its lock is for show: only magic will open it.

details.antagonist: None; the box leads to Fortunata

neighbours.secrets:
Inside (pp. 55-56):
- Principles for a Better Life, tractatus on Principles Lore, Quality 11, Latin
- Heroes of Greece, tractatus on Area Lore: Ancient Greece, Quality 6, Ancient Greek
- Heroes of Greece (revised), tractatus on Area Lore: Ancient Greece, Quality 8, Latin, with added notes
- The Myth of Andros and the Tree, Initiation Script needing a forgotten cult Lore, Script Bonus 12, Ancient Greek
- Andros And the Tree, Principles Lore Initiation Script for Spirit Familiar, Script Bonus 12, Latin

Andros And the Tree opens as a myth of an unnamed hero who beats a monster and frees a maiden caught in a tree, with notes on playing it out in earnest. Intelligence + Magic Lore against 12, or + any Mystery Cult Lore against 6, shows it for an Initiation Script.

Principles for a Better Life reads as a set of good habits, such as rising with the sun and washing in cold water, but is really the Organization Lore of a cult with no members. Its style shows the same hand as the translator of the myth.

Heroes of Greece could pass for Magic or Faerie Lore, but mostly describes land and people. The revised copy says the author lived among the Greek islands, and a seeker might find clues in its notes. All of it is Fortunata's.

neighbours.name: A House in Venice
neighbours.summary: A character, or someone close to one, buys a cheap house in Venice that has stood empty for a while, and finds that earlier owners left in a hurry.
neighbours.secrets: It was Fortunata's, and Lucio still haunts it. See the house's and Lucio's secrets for the rolls and for the hidden papers, which point towards the cluster of islands near hers (p. 56).

neighbours.name: Chrétien the Roamer
neighbours.summary: Among his many disasters, the monk Chrétien tells of a tempest on a voyage out of Venice. He alone survived, cast on the sandy shore of a small island full of strange sights and sounds and airy spirits or ghosts. He lived on crabs and stream water until he had driftwood enough for a raft.
neighbours.secrets: He may recall enough of the ship's storm-driven course to help magi find the island. Adjust where he sailed to the saga's choice of location (p. 57).

neighbours.name: The Witches' Quests
neighbours.summary: Strangers with money approach companions and grogs, buying what they know or hiring them to learn more, about an island no one has heard of.
neighbours.secrets:
The heirs of Cupressa seek the island through agents (p. 57). They may feed characters information so that they find it and are first through its defences, then follow and attack them while they are weak. Or, guarding their search, they may spread false tales that send others on false quests.

See The Heirs of Cupressa.

neighbours.name: Fortunata the Thessalian?
neighbours.summary: Federo of Bonisagus offers a junior magus a reward to follow his leads and prove that Fortunata was a witch of Thessaly, with expeditions to Algiers, Thessaly and the islands where he thinks she lived.

details.antagonist: The Heirs of Cupressa, through false information

neighbours.secrets: The witches have misled him and his quests are misguided, though following them may uncover real truths (p. 57).

neighbours.name: Viea's Legacy
neighbours.summary: Pullatus of Flambeau seeks magi to find the island where, he is sure, Viea lived as Cupressa and raised a half-dragon son. He offers spells for dealing with dragons, texts on Magic Lore (Dragons), and a book of Mediterranean Lore on the area to be searched.

details.antagonist: None; a patron with a theory

neighbours.secrets: As told in Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 6, Trianoma and her sister Viea, sorceresses of Thessaly, woke a dragon that led them to Bonisagus's cave, and Viea quarrelled with her sister and fled before the Order was founded (pp. 57-58). Whether any of Pullatus's theory is true, the book does not say.

neighbours.name: A Vengeful Father
neighbours.summary: Legend tells of the witch, of her son and of the maga who beat them, but not of the father, who is alive and has never learned what happened to them.

stages.title: Curious
stages.clues: He is neutral at first, and curious if offered news of Cupressa.

stages.title: Furious
stages.clues: He learns what befell her and his son.
stages.ignored: If careless, the characters become the first target of his wrath; more likely he flies off after Fortunata.

stages.title: War on the Order
stages.clues: He finds that Fortunata is beyond reach, but that she stood for an Order of magi.
stages.ignored: He blames the whole Order and begins a war against magi.

stages.title: Before the Tribunal
stages.clues: The characters face their sodales, under the Oath's clause against endangering the Order by their actions.

neighbours.secrets: Omaion the Serpent. Anyone looking into Cupressa or Fortunata may cross his path (p. 58). A war he starts falls on those who woke it, under the Oath's clause on endangering the Order.

neighbours.name: Monocaudus's Incitements
neighbours.summary: On the island a monstrous servant pours out a tale of wrongs: the spirit Lucida is a usurper and a jailer, and visitors could right it by standing with him and setting him free.
neighbours.secrets: His stories contradict one another but circle a few themes: that Lucida has imprisoned the other spirits and misuses the mistress's books, and that cruel Fortunata fought and killed his kindly mother. All false. Lucida's scolding may seem to bear him out, but he has earned most of it and overstates the rest (p. 64).

neighbours.name: The Sept of Hérisson
neighbours.summary: The descendants of Hérisson within Clan Arelie of House Bjornaer, who keep his name though their common ancestor is more recent. All hold to the Harmonist cause.
neighbours.secrets: If Hérisson belonged to a hidden Mystery Cult within his House, his heirs may keep it still (p. 72).

neighbours.name: The Field of Copper Urchins
neighbours.summary: A patch of foreign plants set out in sixteen neat rows, in a field with nothing else to remark on: no ruin, no legend, only a faint magic in the ground. In the North they might be rice or orange trees, in the South carrots or turnips.
neighbours.secrets:
The book leaves where this lies to the storyguide. It lies near the characters' covenant, whose vis source it may long have been, or it is won in another story; a weak Magic aura, with no figure given.

Each plant usually bears one offspring holding vis, which grows into the next generation. Now and then one bears two: one may be taken as vis, while the other grows on. The second pawn glows brighter under Sense the Nature of Vis, and only it will grow. In a typical year the sixteen yield two pawns to spare.

Buried here are tiny copper urchins stamped with Hermetic sigils and a chest, turned up by the plough or by magic, holding Hérisson's will. It leaves the fruits of his research to Gypaetus as amends for the bother of killing its discoverer. The notes are not there. A Redcap or a keeper of Tribunal records can tell that Hérisson once claimed this source and that the urchin was his voting sigil, with as much of his story as fits (p. 77).

neighbours.name: Variña's Tomb
neighbours.summary: A lone tower clinging to a mountainside, the sanctum of a Bjornaer maga of the last century. Its ground floor holds only rubbish, and a huge white owl nests on its roof.

levels.name: The ground floor
levels.see: The ground floor of the plain tower, following its outer wall exactly. Deserted, with only rubbish.

levels.name: The hidden cleft
levels.see: A sliver of regio a few feet across, floor to ceiling between one of the ground-floor columns and the outer wall.
levels.notes: Without finding this there is no way on to the third layer.

levels.name: The sepulcher
levels.see: Follows the perimeter of the tower walls on both storeys. An immense stone tomb, with an effigy of enchanted ice under a lasting illusion of the beauty she was.
levels.notes: The tomb may hold a number of magic items of air magic, her specialty; the book names none.

levels.name: The second cleft
levels.see: Another narrow cylinder of regio, in an innocent corner of the upper storey.

levels.name: The upper chamber
levels.see: The upper storey alone, with her laboratory and library.

neighbours.secrets:
High in the Pyrenees, or another fitting range. Finding it may be a story of its own, or the Redcaps may simply have it on record. Each storey lies in a different layer of a regio, so the plain tower hides most of what it holds. The map on pp. 79-80 has its regio boundaries wrong; the text is followed here (errata p. 78).

The owl has lined her nest with parchment from the library, and many of Variña's texts are gone. The storyguide decides how much survives, mostly on Auram. Sorted and restored, Hérisson's notes among the wreck give nothing toward Viresculture, but his diary speaks of a garden like Paradise that is to be his new laboratory once his equipment is moved, and it says plainly where the Garden is.

Intelligence + Area Lore or Order of Hermes Lore then tells a little of that place, chiefly that Caerfloron lies very near: Ease Factor 9 in the same Tribunal, up to 18 across Mythic Europe (pp. 80-81).

neighbours.name: Caerfloron
neighbours.summary: A hortus conclusus: a high-walled garden with a separate hut against the wall for each of its five magi, far from the Order's affairs. The nearest neighbour of a place it does not speak of.
neighbours.secrets:
The book leaves where this lies to the storyguide. A covenant by the book, of Caerfloron and his four filii, with an Aegis of the Hearth of level 20, a weak one; its founding by the Garden is no chance. It has no record as a covenant since this pack keeps none.

Its magi know enough of the Order to fear Wizard's War and not enough to see when the forms were not kept, and they fight by trapping a foe and then making him harmless. They know exactly where the regio opens, and Caerfloron has made a gate that passes its boundary. Each is sworn to enter the Garden but once, and will not say why. Others may use it on one condition, given before they will show the way: their apprentices may go in at the start of training. They will not explain that either; each goes to fetch the mandrake that makes a wizard (p. 83).

neighbours.name: Hérisson's Garden
neighbours.summary:
A paradise close on two miles across, laid out in rings: parkland outermost, then flowery meads, then herb, flower and vegetable gardens, a wooded pleasaunce within, and at the heart a stew, a fish-pond with four streams running to and from it like spokes. The streams make a moat that wanders among the plots under little stone bridges. The ground rolls in hillocks and dells, so the plan is not plain; from high up, streams and hedgerows draw a Hermetic sanctum mark.

Fine weather runs finer here and storms are hushed. Fruit hangs out of season, and no bird or insect sounds, which makes a walk through all that green strangely quiet.

levels.name: The Garden
levels.enter: Through the entrance only the magi of Caerfloron can show, by the gate Caerfloron enchanted.
levels.notes: Magic aura 6 aligned to Herbam: the modifier counts double with the Art of Herbam, and creatures of Herbam Might pay 1 less Might for powers (Realms of Power: Magic p. 16). The aura counts, with its alignment, in the plants' Penetration and Magic Resistance. Two of the stone bridges are enchantments, one keeping the water moving and one keeping it clean.

neighbours.secrets:
The book leaves where this lies to the storyguide. It needs untamed wilderness in a wet temperate Tribunal, or can be recast as a lush oasis in a southern one. Place it near the covenant if it is to stay in the saga, or anywhere if it will be left behind. Caerfloron is close by (pp. 80-81).

The plants. Since Hérisson died the strong aura has twisted the Awakened plants, and they have split into three tribes, each led by a plant that can set its subjects walking. Each leader alone knows where a third of the lore is kept, so nothing can be safely studied until the feud ends. Curtilagium, the kitchen garden, led by Malus: food and medicine plants such as plum, medlar, apricot, apple, orange, leek, carrot, vervain, rosemary, fennel, alexanders and angelica; they fear humans as predators, and are uneasy allies of the Venenarium. Venenarium, the poison garden, led by Mandragora: yew, henbane, foxglove, hellebore, dodder, aconite and many toadstools, with thistles, brambles, holly and hawthorn. Hortulus, the little garden, led by Linum: plants of use and of beauty, such as oak, ash, hazel, pine, rue, hemp, lily, loosestrife, buttercup and mistletoe; they fawn on mankind. See The Battle of the Trees. Mundane plants act only when their leader animates them, with Cunning. The leaders understand speech only by Converse with Plant and Tree (InHe 25) or the like; Intuition of the Forest (InHe 10) gives their moods. They are obstacles or allies more than foes; to harden them make them Summer (240 more experience points) or add 5 to 10 Might with matching Qualities (pp. 84-86).

Warping (p. 88). Perennials of five years or more have a Minor Flaw from warping, and most trees, past 75, have two Minor Flaws and a Minor Virtue: most often (Form) Monstrosity, or Offensive to Animals, Warped Senses or a Personality Flaw. Cinnamon trees may flare at a loud noise; Wrathful brambles wound the more; a rose with Lesser Malediction may blanch in shadow. Plants of his magic bear his spines and thorns.

Enchantments (pp. 88-89), living plants made magic items, which stops their ageing. Bloodthorn, CrCo 15, Pen 0, charged, R Touch D Moon T Ind: a blackthorn whose sloes give +6 to Wound Recovery rolls for a Moon; 4 charges left. (Base 3, +1 Touch, +3 Moon.) Fruitful Medlar, CrHe 9, Pen 0, constant, R Per D Sun T Part: a Lesser Enchantment; a small tree bearing ten times the fruit in season. (Base 1, +2 Sun, +1 Part, +1 size; +1 2/day, +3 environmental trigger.) False Mandrake, PeCo 25, Pen 0, 3/day, R Voice D Mom T Group: a white bryony Prepared with 4 pawns, a small wooden object; touched, it shrieks and deafens all who hear, healing as a Light Wound. (Base 5, +2 Voice, +2 Group; +2 3/day.) Traveling Thistle, CrVi 14, Pen 0, constant, R Per D Mom T Ind (the level sum uses Sun, p. 88): a faint taint of magic that its seedlings inherit but do not pass on; the key to self-replicating vis. (Base 3, +2 Sun, +1 inherited; +1 2/day, +3 environmental trigger.) Creeping Buttercup, ReVi 20, Pen 0, 1/day, R Per D Mom T Part: holds a pawn of Herbam vis and once in its life may pass it to a seed, whose plant has the same power. (Base 10, +1 Part, +1 special effect.) Everlasting Orpine: an orpine with a red stem and pinkish-red crown, Prepared with 6 pawns of Vim vis, a Medium wooden object; living, but stopped and sterile; an Insight worth 2 Breakthrough points. Ever-Flowering Bramble, CrHe 33, Pen 0, 1/day, R Per D Sun T Ind: a blackberry seed grows, fruits, seeds and dies in a day, and its seed does so the next, giving a handful of good fruit; leave one berry or it ends. (Base 15, +2 Sun, +1 special effect; +3 environmental trigger.) Hazel of Many Tools, ReHe 5, Pen 0, charged, R Per D Mom T Ind: name a tool and a twig takes its shape to be broken off; Intelligence + Finesse, Ease Factor 9, for standard quality; craft magic, 10 charges left. (Base 5, Covenants p. 51.)

Stirpes (p. 89), invigoration exhausted, each bearing a single magical offspring a generation, itself a Stirps: Adder's Tongue (Perdo, in the curled central leaf); Alexanders (Herbam, in the stems); Ever-Burning Fire (Ignem, flames in the Fennel of Herbam Vis, derived from a fire elemental); Harebell (Animal, the furred flower); Pasternack, a purple carrot (Aquam, in the roots); Selfheal (Creo); Silverweed (Terram, leaves of real silver). One pawn each. Several uninvigorated, immortal cultivars grow here too.

Lesser Enchantment Vis (p. 89), Stirpes likewise exhausted; to Invigorate them needs Hérisson's Minor Breakthrough again. Daisy of Intellego Vis, InHe 40, Pen 16, 3/day, R Touch D Conc T Ind: the toucher converses with plants as Converse with Plant and Tree, Penetrating any Resistance of the plant. (Base 15, +1 Touch, +1 Conc; +5 maintains concentration, +2 3/day, +8 Penetration 16.) Mistletoe Sprig of Herbam Vis: Realms of Power: Magic p. 121. Stinking Hellebore of Rego Vis, ReCo 25, Pen 0, unlimited, R Touch D Diam T Ind: touching its fleshy green flowers paralyzes for two minutes; p. 87 calls it of Corpus Vis. (Base 5, +1 Touch, +1 Diam; +10 unlimited uses.) Honeysuckle of Mentem Vis, ReMe 24, Pen 0, constant, R Per D Sun T Scent: a vine of hooked yellow flowers; as Confusion of the Numbed Will on all who smell it, about 6 paces out. (Base 4, +2 Sun, +2 Scent; +1 2/day, +3 environmental trigger.) Fennel of Herbam Vis, Re(Cr)Ig(He) 24, Pen 0, constant, R Per D Sun T Ind: +5 Soak against fire, whose damage heals at once; it hosts the Ever-Burning Fire. (Base 4, +2 Sun, +2 requisites; +1 2/day, +3 environmental trigger.)

Enriched Herbs of Virtue (pp. 89-90; Realms of Power: Magic p. 124), preserved until used. Henbane of Virtue: a pawn of Perdo vis. Three Enriched capsules lie by the stem; a capsule steeped in scorpion venom and three crushed owl skulls under Saturn ascendant, then swallowed after a season, gives Lesser Immunity to Poison and numbs a sense or limb (simple die: 1-2 Afflicted Tongue, 3-4 Poor Eyesight, 5-6 Poor Hearing, 7-8 Missing Hand, 9-10 Lame), for a year. Wild Teasel of Virtue: two pawns of Corpus in the juice; fed to a pregnant dog, her litter's milk-teeth ground into wine give Puissant Brawl, Tough, Berserk and Wrathful for a year or until the drinker tastes valerian juice. Valerian of Virtue: two pawns of Creo in the root; sliced with silver on a night Venus shows, bathed in horse urine each Friday and ground between amber, it gives Rapid Convalescence, Enduring Constitution, Reserves of Strength and a Code of Honor for a year or until the drinker tastes teasel milk.

Wrestling in the Herb Garden (p. 90). Teasel and valerian grow thick on either side of a sward, split by a thin line of grass. Touch a patch and the urge to fight whoever explores the other takes hold; one champion is picked for each. Teasel's fights dirty, for many small wounds; valerian's grapples and pins. Whoever beats the teasel's man gets a draft of Enriched Teasel Milk, and whoever beats the valerian's a sip of Enriched Valerian Juice.

Wonders (p. 91), among over fifty fine or unique species. The Vegetable Lamb: four feet tall, each stem tipped with a tiny woolly lamb that grazes around the plant, then, the grass gone, dwindles to a ball of wool. A cinnamon grove, pungent and apt to ignite. A child of the Drudenbaum of Harberg (Guardians of the Forests p. 89) that yields no vis. Perhaps Soqotran totem trees (Rival Magic): cinnabar, olibanum, myrrh and aloe. Add more with Realms of Power: Magic.

Rediscovery (pp. 91-92). Hérisson went by Original Research, 45 Breakthrough points for the Major and 30 for the Minor. A magus here need not: his inventions serve as sources of Insight (Ancient Magic p. 8, Hedge Magic p. 14), and duplicating an effect earns points equal to its magnitude. His living enchantments are read by Investigating in the laboratory in place of Intelligence + Magic Theory. So are his Stirpes, each as an enchantment of level 15, the Insight being a version of Gather the Essence of the Beast: 3 points the first time and 1 for each later version. Other plants of the Garden use Ancient Magic's process, and the Minor Breakthrough must draw on these, after Viresculture itself is regained. At the storyguide's option Lab Texts of his creations lie here (p. 92), giving their magnitude once studied by recreating the experiment (True Lineages p. 29): a tree with a page on each leaf, to be put in order; a fruit written on its seeds.

Study (p. 92). Realia for Herbam (Covenants p. 102), Source Quality 6, six times in all. For one who has Hermetic Viresculture the Stirpes are realia of it, Quality 4, four times.

Laboratory (pp. 92-94). The Garden is a working Hermetic laboratory; adapt it as Taking Over a Laboratory (Covenants p. 118). Hérisson lived there as a beast, so a tenant needs a hut. Virtues: Natural Environment (Major, Structure); Lesser Feature, the spring that aids vis extraction (Minor, Structure); Specimens x3 and Superior Decorations (Minor, Outfitting; no extra Upkeep, being alive); Spacious (Minor, Structure); Vis Source (Minor, Supernatural); Idyllic Surroundings (Free, Structure); Inexhaustible Supplies (Free, Supernatural); Regio (Free, Supernatural). Flaws: Outdoors (Major, Structure); Chaotic and Living (Minor, Supernatural); Disorganized (Free, Structure). Characteristics: Size +10 (+5), Refinement 0, General Quality -1, Upkeep -1, Safety -5, Warping +6, Health 0, Aesthetics +6. Specializations: Vis Extraction +3, Experimentation +2, Herbam +10, Imaginem +1, Muto +2. Traits: Growing +3, Curious +2, Exotic +1.

Its tools grow: gourds for flasks, fungi for bowls, branches over rocks for benches, birch-bark for paper, the Ever-Burning Tree for fire (so p. 93; p. 89 has the Ever-Burning Fire), the brook for water. When planning a season roll a simple die: under the Warping Characteristic the means are to hand; otherwise choose another activity. Add 2 in winter. A truce with the plants adds Lesser Horde (Supernatural, no Upkeep): +1 General Quality, Safety and Aesthetics, +1 in Perdo (Venenarium), Creo (Curtilagium) or Rego (Hortulus). A tribe made an enemy adds Gremlins: -3 Safety, +1 Warping, -1 Aesthetics, +1 Experimentation, +1 in that same Art.

neighbours.name: The Search for Hérisson's Garden
neighbours.summary: Spiny plants full of vis keep turning up around the covenant, and a buried will points to the lost research of a legendary magus. Someone else wants it badly.

stages.title: Foreshadowing
stages.clues: Now and then, among unrelated stories, magical plants turn up in one region as stray pawns of vis, perhaps Spell-Like or Lesser Enchantment Vis: escapees from his early research, bristling with his spines and thorns. See The Basilisk Rose and A Gruit Local Custom.

stages.title: The buried will
stages.clues: The field's foreign plants in their neat rows, copper urchins, and a chest with Hérisson's will. A Redcap or Tribunal archivist supplies his story. Two trails follow: his heirs, and his slayer's line.

stages.title: Hérisson's descendants
stages.clues: Tasso Agricola tells the legend and offers copies of his ciphered texts for a share of what is found. Records show Gypaetus died in 1035, leaving only Variña.
stages.ignored: Strabo soon hears from Tasso of the characters' interest, and may have them attacked before they have learned anything.

stages.title: Variña's Tomb
stages.clues: The tower's nested regio, the owl, and the parchment in her nest, with the Garden's location in Hérisson's diary.

stages.title: The ambush
stages.clues: By now Strabo knows the magi and their home. Local ruffians fall on them on the road and take what they can to a distant tavern, where Strabo pays them with poison after he has the goods.
stages.ignored: He may flood the covenant with quick-growing ivy while, as one strand of it, he searches the magi's belongings; or just follow them and race ahead to Caerfloron once he sees the way they go.

stages.title: Caerfloron
stages.clues: The five magi meet the characters with open hostility or an outright assault of Herbam magic: Strabo has told them a Wizard's War is coming. Warned in time, he has even served a false declaration, disguised as a local Redcap by Disguise of the New Visage, without knowing the Garden lies here if he has not seen the notes.
stages.stopped: Neither side knows why the other is fighting, so a parley can show the lie. Strabo flees and is outside the Code, liable to a Wizard's March. Caerfloron makes amends by showing the way in, once promised the right to send apprentices in.

stages.title: Into the Garden
stages.clues: The gate opens on the regio, and the feud of the plants begins. See The Battle of the Trees.

neighbours.secrets: In Search of Eden (pp. 76-83). Reaching the Garden lets the characters rebuild Hermetic Viresculture by Insights, far quicker and safer than Original Research. Strabo needs the same notes, so he stays ahead of them until unmasked. He does not want the magi killed at first, only what they carry.

neighbours.name: The Battle of the Trees
neighbours.summary: The arrival of strangers sets the old feud of the Garden's plants alight, and something is watching them from the grass.

stages.title: Watched
stages.clues: Curtilagium and Hortulus observe the strangers. Only Magic Sensitivity may catch beings with Might among the Garden's general magic. Eating the fruit and gathering vis rouses the Curtilagium.

stages.title: The night camp
stages.clues: A fire brings Malus's hardwoods trampling through the camp. Mandragora rings it in the night with a hedge of bramble and hawthorn, as Wall of Thorns. Afterward toadstools line the paths and crowd each resting place, and the silence presses in.

stages.title: The buttercup path
stages.clues: On the second day a path of creeping buttercup appears where none was and leads to Linum's meadow. It needs magic to be understood; it points those without any to a Daisy of Intellego Vis. It welcomes them, excuses the Curtilagium as fearful, urges them to convince Malus, and will not mention the Venenarium.

stages.title: The orchard
stages.clues: Linum can direct them to Malus, but Mandragora has convinced it they mean to destroy the Garden. Mandragora sends animated Stinking Hellebore to paralyze them; Malus binds them in honeysuckle and ivy, as Trap of the Entwining Vines; failing that, it thickens the undergrowth to shield itself.

stages.title: The source of the poison
stages.clues: If they find Mandragora out it sends Dodder against the strongest of them, and keeps its Deadly Scream until it is in direct peril; that is deadly to those without Magic Resistance, and readily answered by those with it.
