stages.stopped: A truce opens the lore of all three tribes and gives the laboratory its Lesser Horde.
stages.turned: A tribe made an enemy brings Gremlins on the laboratory.

neighbours.secrets:
Pp. 86-87. The Garden cannot be properly explored until the tribes make peace; the plants vital to the research belong to all three, and each leader's help is needed. Do not show the tribes merely as monsters to kill. Mandragora feeds Malus's fear; while it does, there can be no peace with the Curtilagium, and attacks by both tribes go on at random. The book gives no set way to end the feud. Finding the Mistletoe of Herbam Vis early gives a feel for the plants.

The cruelest trick: kill a grog in secret and send Dodder in the corpse to walk among his friends.

neighbours.name: The Basilisk Rose
neighbours.summary: An important noble's daughter is sick with something no physician can name. Her one comfort is the scent of a gray and pink rose found only in her garden, of which a fresh bloom is brought to her each day.

details.antagonist: A noble with a poisoner's secret

neighbours.secrets:
A Wreath of Pale Flowers (pp. 76-77). The rose is an escaped cultivar of Hérisson, one of his few destructive ones, with Perdo vis in it. Its roots taint her water, and its blossoms ease the poison, so uprooting it surely kills her.

Her father planted the rose in a nearby town some years ago to rid himself of opponents by a false plague, then felled it, not knowing a seed had reached his daughter's garden. No one has connected the plague with the rose. Who gave him the plant is left open: a demon tempting him to murder, a magus with a grudge against the town, or a faerie hoping to gain vitality as the girl's rescuer.

neighbours.name: A Gruit Local Custom
neighbours.summary: Each year a village the covenant trades with holds a contest for best brew, between the delicate ale of the Marianne Sisters, loved by the women, and the heavy acorn and bog-myrtle beer of Lorris Taverner, loved by the men. Both keep their recipes close, and passions run high. The magi are asked to judge.

stages.title: The verdict
stages.clues: The whole village holds its breath; its pride and output hang on it.
stages.stopped: Meddling with either brewing earns the enmity of the whole village.
stages.turned: For the ale: the men turn hostile, and the women's cottage industries gain. For the beer: crops get a small boost for the year, and the women turn sullen and bad-mouth the characters.

neighbours.secrets: P. 77. Both drinks carry a faint taint of magic. The elder Marianne sister is Touched by Magic (City & Guild p. 71) and flavors her gruit with hyssop grown in a Magic aura. Lorris has no magic, but owns one of Hérisson's oaks: its acorns, known by the spines on their cups, hold at least a pawn of Imaginem vis, more in a good year.

neighbours.name: A Dangerous Tithe
neighbours.summary: Grain does not grow unseen. The local priest has noticed that the covenant farms, and comes for a tenth of whatever God gives increase, with a reeve to see he is not cheated.
neighbours.secrets: P. 76. A story seed of a covenant using Hermetic Viresculture. The tithe in theory covers vis, so the characters must give up vis whose magic they would not put in anyone's hands, least of all the Church's.

neighbours.name: Like Nothing I've Ever Tasted
neighbours.summary: Something has been eating from the covenant's strange field, or its livestock has been poached.
neighbours.secrets: P. 76. A story seed of a covenant using Hermetic Viresculture. A peasant eats a crop or beast of Lesser Enchantment Vis and gains its effect, perhaps for good, at the cost of Warping. He must be found before he tells others and they all come for the precious Stirpes.

neighbours.name: A Burning Desire
neighbours.summary: A phoenix near the end of its life comes to the Garden seeking a cinnamon tree for its last nest.
neighbours.secrets: P. 93. It builds a nest of cinnamon boughs for the rising sun to light, and a chick is reborn in the ashes. A magus wanting a rare familiar may bargain for the chick. The price is the death of a far-off king with a taste for exotic birds. To ignore the deal after the parent dies, or put it off, invokes the phoenix's death-curse.

neighbours.name: The Kidnapped Totems
neighbours.summary: After centuries of searching, a delegation of foreign sorcerers forces its way into the Garden.
neighbours.secrets: P. 93; Rival Magic chapter 3. Hérisson stole the Soqotrans' totem plants, a theft like kidnapping a loved one, that has cost generations of would-be sorcerers their power. One from each tribe comes to take back the trees and punish the thief. They will take Hermetic magi in the Garden for his heirs, since they use his magic, and vent their fury on them before they go.

neighbours.name: The Aquatic Valley
neighbours.summary:
A shallow valley on the sea floor off the south coast of Crete, of barnacled rock and gently sloping sand, strewn with the broken ships of an ancient battle. By day shafts of sunlight fall from the surface and move across the sand. It is very beautiful. Among the wrecks dozens of pale sailors go on fighting, day after day, as they have for fifteen hundred years. The water holds more light than its depth should allow.

Rules. Magic aura 2. Depth 14 paces at the laboratory complex. Swimmers move at half walking speed; only thrusting weapons, or those where speed is no matter, work well, others suffering heavy penalties if they work at all. Trained groups do not carry over between land and water. Vision blurs, and only very large things show past 20 paces. Unaided, spells are cast with no words and subtle gestures, at the usual penalties, and a Voice range spell cast submerged reaches only targets in or touching the surface. After each 10 paces of descent a character loses, in Fatigue levels, a tenth of current depth minus Soak (armor not counted). Spells for going under water: Lungs of the Fish (ArM5 p. 122), Maris of Tytalus's creations (Magi of Hermes pp. 70-78), and here Cloak of Fins and Scales, Form of the Aquatic Predator and Shape of the Siren (p. 105-106), Breeze from Within and Eyes of the Fish (p. 106). Those transformed into fish suffer no pressure penalties. The Order holds such devices and Lab Texts, and a determined magus may bargain for them.

The Ring of Aquatic Freedom (p. 106): a lesser enchanted device with Beyond Reach of the Sea, ReAq 34, constant effect, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Part. Water stays 6 paces from the ring; the wearer cannot drink, and sweat is thrown from the body.
neighbours.secrets:
The battle was fought between Demetrios the Poliorketes and Ptolemy I; the book dates it 306 BC on p. 99 and 309 BC on p. 101. Near the center of the valley lies a wreck with no ghosts on it. On it stands Hermanus' wooden mannequin, human-sized, gripping the mast, which is waterlogged but wholly free of rot and holds 8 pawns of Mentem vis. Hermanus' last spell pins both in place, against nearly any physical force.

The return. Any spell aimed at either object (to move it, an Intellego spell, Rego Vim to draw the vis) undoes that spell and brings the laboratory structure back. All water within thirteen paces is thrust out, with sand and debris; swimmers are carried at least 20 paces unless they act against it. Characters not submerged should not be crushed. Stirred sediment blinds for a few minutes. A storyguide who wants the laboratory won rather than handed over can have the characters fetch it from the Twilight Void: Arcane Connections do not cross from the mundane world, so they must find a way into the Magic Realm (Realms of Power: Magic chapter three; p. 104).

Moving the story (p. 101). Ancient naval battles fit, more or less as written, across the Mediterranean: Actium, 31 BC, in the Ionian Sea; Alalia off Corsica, 540 BC. North of it, Carlingford Loch, Ireland, where Norse and Danes fought three days in 852. A storyguide may invent a battle old enough to be unrecorded, or drop the water: the mannequin could lie in a regio of huge ice caves, a Saharan oasis, or the player covenant's best vis source, if that was claimed after 1098.

neighbours.name: The Sunken Laboratory of Hermanus
neighbours.summary: A single-story disk of a building some 35 paces across and three and a half tall, stone-walled and wooden-roofed, shuttered on all sides, with one door ajar. It sits level on the sea floor, wreck and shards of lower floors scattered round it, in a sphere of dry space the water does not enter. Nothing in it has aged a day since 1098.
neighbours.secrets:
Until the return it lies in the Terram province of the Twilight Void, tethered to the mannequin and mast in the Aquatic Valley; the fragments of lower floors hold nothing of value. No aura is printed for the structure. Seven rooms, each a record here: hallway, scriptorium and store room on the outer ring; receiving room, spare laboratory, sanctum (room 6) and laboratory (room 7).

Sentinels and justiciars. Sentinels are devices with Intellego effects and Herald of Imperative, which fires the justiciars of the room; justiciars incapacitate. Built for a covenant where people live, they mostly imprison rather than kill. At Coeris other devices report any firing, so even one that fails to penetrate raises the alarm. Many of these devices are copies of those guarding Coeris.

Herald of Imperative: ReVi 29, 50/day, R: Touch, D: Mom, T: Room. Performs one fixed triggering action on every object in the room. (Base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Room; +6 levels 50 uses, +3 levels linked trigger.) Rego Vim guideline, level 5: activate a device with a simple trigger, the caster knowing the action; the item fires directly (p. 107).

The justiciar action. Every justiciar here, and at Coeris, uses one long, complex action of delicate handling and exact intonation: three rounds by hand, days of intense study to learn. It can be written down from the Herald's Lab Texts or by laboratory investigation of a sentinel or justiciar. The House keeps all other texts of it in the Coeris vaults; the ones here are the only others. An outsider who knows it weakens Coeris badly, which is the House's real concern. The vexillation argued over one action or many: one was easier to monitor and rearrange, and magi of the work were vetted by Intellego.

A Modification (Penetration, frequency, triggers, effect use) does not count toward whether an effect warps its target, so Alarm of Dissemblance, say, does not (p. 112).

Balance (p. 117; errata p. 78). Challenging, not impossible, avoiding the trivial and the merely annoying. For impatient or weaker groups, less active spirits or clues in Amarantha's notes; for strong ones, more than two elemental spirits, or greater Might. Players should see that disturbing the rings in the outer rooms may flood at least those rooms.

Riches (p. 119), besides the devices and the laboratory: 6 pawns of Rego, 18 of Mentem and 8 of Vim vis. Lab Texts for every enchantment on the laboratory and every device in it, all sentinels and justiciars of this chapter, and the Ring and Circle wards active here, including Circular Ward Against Magical Spirits. A casting tablet (Covenants pp. 89-90) of Cargo of Angel's Wings, printed R: Arc, which Hermanus used through a spell like Opening the Intangible Tunnel to fetch vis and connections from his mannequin.

neighbours.name: Laboratory of Hermanus: Hallway
neighbours.summary: A curved passage stripped of the trophies and records that once praised the Adamant Rook, with a thin rug, a chandelier of half-burnt candles, and a small table bearing a locked chest with a little marble statue of a man on it. Four doors. Steel bands run along the outer wall, and a few inches of sea water cling where it meets floor and ceiling.
neighbours.secrets:
The doors: north, just under two paces high, to the sea floor, where water stands like a wall; a like door on the inside wall at the south end; and at each end a floor-to-ceiling door, flush with the outer wall so a caster can trace the rings. All but the outer are locked.

Bands in the hallway, scriptorium and store room hold the outer wards: Ward Against Water (ReAq 20, cast forcelessly, Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 72, so Penetration 0, and magi and creatures with Magic Resistance carry their liquids through; others wet or sweating are slowed as water is stripped off them); Circular Ward Against Demons, level 40, Penetration 37; Circular Ward Against Faerie Spirits, level 40, Penetration 35, so Might 34 or lower. Rings can be reached over the small doors.

Locksmith's Will (sentinel), on the north door: a lead horseshoe, opened with 6 pawns, filled. Lock Improperly Opened, InTe 29, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room: fires the Herald when a lock in the room, walls and doors included, is opened without its key, whether picked, by magic or smashed.

Statue of Conjured Assistants: hand-sized marble, like the statues in the sanctum. Summon the Stony Servants, ReTe 52, Penetration 8, 6/day, R: Arc, D: Mom, T: Group, Arcane Connections built in: brings Ferox and Fidelius to the statue. Any improper opening here does so.

In the locked chest: a silver ring holding 2 pawns of Vim vis.

neighbours.name: Laboratory of Hermanus: Scriptorium
neighbours.summary: Writing desks, quills, parchment and the tools of scribes and illuminators along the inner wall, with nothing in hand on them. A tall door at each end; the steel bands and clinging water run on through.
neighbours.secrets:
The work in hand was taken away that evening at Hermanus' request, before he raised his defenses.

Handle of Ill Will (sentinel), on the door to the store room: opened with 10 pawns, 9 filled. Test of Motive, InMe 60, Penetration +60, unlimited, R: Touch, D: Mom, T: Ind: whoever touches the handle, asks whether they wish House Tremere ill fortune, and fires the Herald if so.

Net of Patient Thieves (justiciar), tied under a desk: a tiny bronze net, charged, 11 charges, usually hidden so victims cannot reach it. Elevation of the Interloper, ReCo 65, Penetration +60, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room: all people in the room float a few inches clear of floor and walls until next dawn or dusk, stuck unless they can move without touching anything.

neighbours.name: Laboratory of Hermanus: Store Room
neighbours.summary: Full of sweet-smelling smoke that hardly hides anything. Shelves on the inner wall are packed with laboratory equipment, and among it stand two wooden mannequins in chain hauberks with polearms and crossbows. The steel bands and clinging water continue here.
neighbours.secrets:
Censer of the Unseen (sentinel), rock crystal, on the shelves: opened with 8 pawns, printed with one pawn free. Room of Pleasant Incense, CrAu 9, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Ind: smoke fills the room but no further, and those with Magic Resistance cannot smell it. Ascertaining the Absence of Images, InIm 34, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room: fires the Herald if any space holds no image of smoke or object, as an invisible being does, or if all the smoke is cleared.

Pebble of the Stone Prison (justiciar), a polished river pebble on the shelves, lesser device. Box of Stone, CrTe 16, 2/day, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Ind: a foot of stone lines floor, walls and ceiling, between the room and its contents, pushing things a foot inward; things with Magic Resistance are not moved but left in holes in the stone. Things fixed to the room stay outside it. Self-supporting, but its great weight needs footing: a foolish choice for an upper floor, though the room now rests on the seabed.

neighbours.name: Laboratory of Hermanus: Receiving Room
neighbours.summary: Chairs, tables and cabinets, where the Adamant Rook once met, and where Hermanus later saw magi he would not admit further. A copper bowl and a carved wooden box sit on the middle table, and two staves tipped with silver eyes lean on the inner wall. The north door bears the sanctum symbol; a door-sized patch of different stonework marks the old way to the laboratory.
neighbours.secrets:
Ferox and Fidelius have likely taken the staves before the party comes. If either is here it may lie on purpose to spring the room.

Ear of Truth (sentinel), the copper bowl: invested, 10 pawns, printed filled. Alarm of Dissemblance, InMe 55, Penetration 34, unlimited, R: Touch, D: Diam, T: Room: fires the Herald on any lie told here. The limit of the Infernal keeps it from working on demons.

Box of Vines (justiciar), a carved box the size of a loaf, lesser device. Chamber of Thorns, CrHe 16, 2/day, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Group: in a flash, thorny bushes fill the room, around all within. Soak +15; only edged weapons cut them, a Heavy wound a pace. Forcing through: Strength stress roll, Ease Factor 9 a pace, +15 damage either way, 5 more on a botch.

Staff of the Wooden Soldiers. An invested device, a thick hazel staff topped with a silver eye, with a small chamber near the top for an Arcane Connection to one mannequin. Opened with 14 pawns, all filled. Four powers, each 12 a day, item maintains concentration, R: Arc, D: Conc: Pretense of Humanity (MuIm 19, T: Ind), the mannequin looks like a person of its size; Animate Mannequin (ReHe 34, T: Ind), it moves as the holder commands, with the holder's Dexterity, Quickness and Abilities and Strength +3; View from the Mannequin and Ears of the Mannequin (each InIm 34, T: special, based on Room), the holder's sight or hearing moves to the mannequin, seeing or hearing even creatures with Magic Resistance, and into adjacent rooms and out of windows (p. 112-113).

A blow of damage 10 or more takes a limb off a mannequin, 19 or more on the armored ones of the complex. Melee weapons they swing are resisted by Magic Resistance; crossbow bolts are not, not being driven by magic. Each mannequin's detachable wooden feature serves as the Arcane Connection, changed regularly at Coeris; those here have not decayed, as no time passed in the Void.

These two staves hold the right ears of the spare laboratory's mannequins.

neighbours.name: Laboratory of Hermanus: Spare Laboratory
neighbours.summary: Hermanus' workroom while the vexillation lasted, left for the larger room when it ended. A table holds an hourglass of crystal and limestone and a silver candlestick. Two wooden mannequins in full chain stand ready with polearms and crossbows, each missing its right ear.
neighbours.secrets:
Hourglass of Airy Trespass (sentinel): opened with 11 pawns. Sense the Airy Trespass, InVi 50 (errata p. 78; printed 75), Penetration +32, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room: fires the Herald every round a being of Magic Might 31 or lower is present. The book says the two effects fill the 11 pawns; that was before the correction.

Prison of Audacious Spirits (justiciar), the candlestick, so named on p. 113 though once called Prison of Insubstantial Spirits: charged, 7 charges. Insubstantial Prison, ReVi 71, Penetration 30, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room: creatures of Magic Might 30 or less cannot cross the room's bounds, nor can their powers, until it ends or is dispelled. Not limited to spirits.

neighbours.name: Laboratory of Hermanus: Sanctum
neighbours.summary: The door opens on a wall of wood, flush with the frame, dented where the handle sat. Cleared, the room is richly furnished: fine tapestries, a bed, a dresser, a desk, and two foot-and-a-half granite statues of men. Two wooden mannequins stand by.
neighbours.secrets:
Charm of the Herbam Padlock, a small silver ring on the floor by the laboratory door, where Hermanus left it: opened with 6 pawns, filled, made for the Coeris vaults, kept active there. Chamber of Heartwood, CrHe 29, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Ind: one block of wood fills the room, snug round its contents, on touching the door with the charm. Insubstantial Wooden Foundation, ReHe 24, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Ind: holds the block and keeps its weight off the floor.

Two sentinels and one justiciar. Drawing a metal weapon without the House Tremere symbol, or touching the carpet while believing the House would disapprove of one's plans, fires the turtle.

Ward against Foreign Steel (sentinel), a marble apple behind a chest by the bed: 8 pawns, filled. React to Naked Blades, InTe(Im) 45, Penetration 42, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room. Coeris grogs carry marked weapons, but visiting Tremere have had accidents.

Carpet of Loyalty (sentinel), under the desk: an embroidered square rug about 2 paces across, showing Tremere and Guernicus, silver wires in the border; 9 pawns, filled. Interrogation of Interlopers, InMe 60, Penetration +60, unlimited, R: Touch, D: Mom, T: Ind: asks whoever touches it if the House's members would disapprove of their plans. Those with no idea what the Tremere think do not fire it.

Turtle of Welcome Reflection (justiciar), a jet figurine in the northwest corner: charged, 11 charges. Armoring the Intruder, MuCo(An) 60, Penetration +50, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room: humans and others subject to Corpus spells become turtles until next sunrise or sunset.

Oracle-Countering Tapestry, on the wall right of the door from the receiving room, lesser device, one of several copies. Masking the Magical Chamber, PeVi 45, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room: Hermetic Intellego Vim cannot detect magic here below level 53.

This third pair of mannequins is out of the spirits' reach until the block is gone, and even then they must get Arcane Connections to the staves.

neighbours.name: Laboratory of Hermanus: Laboratory
neighbours.summary: A tapestry hangs just past the door. Behind it a deep workbench runs round half the circular room, shelved to the ceiling with carpenters' and jewelers' tools. Eight rings of metal, stone and brick are set in the floor behind it. In the middle stand tables of equipment, a desk and many tomes of notes, and on one table a silver-eyed staff and a small wooden doll. The plaster ceiling shows the night sky reversed, black stars on white, and brass wires carry hooked spheres marked for the planets.
neighbours.secrets:
Rings: Circular Ward Against Demons, level 40, Penetration 35; Ring of Warding Against Spirits, level 30, Penetration 40; Circular Ward Against Magical Spirits, level 40, Penetration 36; Circular Ward Against Faerie Spirits, level 40, Penetration 37; Ward Against Faeries of the Water, level 25, Penetration 30; Ward Against the Beasts of Legend, level 30, Penetration 30; Circle of Beast Warding; Ward Against Water.

As a laboratory (Covenants chapter nine): Size +1, Refinement +6, and when working General Quality +3, Upkeep +4, Aesthetics +5, with +6 item creation, +1 texts, +1 Intellego, +1 Imaginem. Virtues: Greater Feature (workbench), Lesser Feature (ceiling), Greater Expansion, Highly Organized, Superior Lighting (the Orb). A Laboratory record needs a covenant, so it is kept here in words.

Staff of the Wooden Soldiers: as in the Receiving Room; this one holds a connection to the remains of the sea-floor mannequin. The doll is a fixed Arcane Connection to that mannequin.

Tapestry of Confident Possession (sentinel), silver-ornamented, covering about a third of the walls, so that entering or reaching many cabinets and books means moving it: invested, 16 pawns, 10 filled. Assurance of Ownership, InMe 65, Penetration 50, unlimited, R: Touch, D: Mom, T: Room: on moving it, fires the Herald if any mind present does not believe the laboratory is its own.

Cross of the Preempted Conflict (justiciar), a small metal cross: charged, 13 charges. Beneficent Gift of Loyalty, ReMe 65, Penetration +40, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room: those present must do all they can to guard the laboratory, its contents and above all its rightful owners. Who those are is now arguable; Ferox and Fidelius will say House Tremere, and the characters may differ. None under it will let anything be taken from the complex. The vexillation hoped thieves would give themselves up.

Butterfly's Gaze, a six-inch silver butterfly with ivory inlay on the wall: invested, 15 pawns. Gaze of Maker's Mark, InVi 49, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room: seeks magic without Hermanus' sigil, the embattled lines. Counter Intruding Magics, PeVi 63, unlimited, R: Special, D: Mom, T: Ind: dispels it if its level doubled is met by stress die + 55, once a round, target chosen at random, when a targeted spell enters or is cast. A Momentary spell may take effect first.

Wolf's Gaze, a six-inch silver wolf's head on the wall: invested, 6 pawns, 5 filled. Awareness of Fire, InIg 14, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Room: triggers Protection of Cool and Dark, PeIg 28, unlimited, R: Touch, D: Mom, T: Room, putting out fires of +5 damage per exposure or less (ArM5 p. 181).

Orb of Obedient Sunlight, a gold-colored wooden sphere on the wires, lesser device. Obedient Sunlight, CrIg 20, unlimited, item maintains concentration, R: Per, D: Conc, T: Ind: bright light on command, against fire and open windows.

Helm of Unravelling, a steel helmet, 12 pawns, for grogs to break enemy magic; Coeris's trusted grogs carry but rarely wear them, for Sight of Forming Spells warps. Sight of Forming Spells, InVi 60, Penetration +32, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Vision: magic shows as a violet glow, strongest in casting, not old residues. Shout of Unravelling, PeVi 60, Penetration +32, 12/day, R: Voice, D: Mom, T: Ind: shouted while staring at a power or effect; dispels if its level doubled is met by stress die + 50, and can counter a spell cast later in the round. Neither works past Magic Resistance it does not penetrate.

On the room itself. Opened by Hermanus in its walls with 20 pawns, 15 filled. Foreboding of Stones, InTe 19, constant, R: Pers, D: Sun, T: Hearing: senses a solid thing about to strike hard enough to do damage, and triggers Skin of the Sapphire Tortoise, MuTe(He) 35, unlimited, R: Pers, D: Diam, T: Room: walls, floor or ceiling as hard as gemstone and tough as iron. Protection of the Mason's Vision, ReTe(He) 28, unlimited, R: Pers, D: Mom, T: Special: puts back any part of the structure removed, up to 5 paces out; rubble cannot reassemble. Invisible Eye Uncovered, InVi(Im) 45, constant, R: Pers, D: Sun, T: Room: shows any magical spying of up to level 52 as a flickering image in the room.

neighbours.name: The Remains of Amarantha
neighbours.summary:
Old bones and a large leather satchel, the one thing about them untouched by decay. Within: an apple, cheese and bread, and a bundle of notes.

The book leaves the place open: somewhere remote that might hold vis, such as a regio, wilderness that could host a vis site, or what might have been a creature of might's lair in Hermanus' day. It can be worked into another adventure of the saga.
neighbours.secrets:
The satchel (p. 100): a lesser enchanted device of Amarantha's own. Enchantment of Incorruptible Vellum, CrAn(He) 24, constant, R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Group: guards it and its animal and plant contents from natural decay. Long exposure has warped satchel and contents: the food cannot be digested and sickens anyone who tries it, and bare skin that touches leather or notes takes a mild rash.

The notes take about a day to read. They say who she was and what she was about; sum up Hermanus' life and habits; tell of the mannequin, a fixed Arcane Connection, sent about the world and run by spells through Opening the Intangible Tunnel; say the laboratory surely held much vis, and that the House badly wants the texts and devices for what they reveal of Coeris's defenses; and give a part-checked list of sites.

The list is long, but a century of Hermetic work has ruled out most of it. Checked against House Mercere's lists of covenants and claimed vis sources it falls to a short list, or to the true site alone, as the storyguide wishes.

neighbours.name: The Search for the Sunken Laboratory
neighbours.summary: A dead Tremere's satchel points to the lost wing of Coeris: a hoard of vis and devices, if it can be found, raised and entered.

stages.title: Amarantha's notes
stages.clues: The characters come on her remains and satchel, best within another adventure (The Remains of Amarantha; the place is left to the storyguide). Her list of sites shrinks against House Mercere's records.

stages.title: The sea floor off Crete
stages.clues: After perhaps trying other sites, they reach the Aquatic Valley and the trials of working under water.

stages.title: The valley's guardians
stages.clues: The genius loci guards the ships and ghosts, and the ghosts take newcomers for friend or foe.

stages.title: The laboratory returns
stages.clues: A spell on the mannequin or mast brings the structure back. Inside, they must outwit its seven rooms of defenses and Ferox and Fidelius to reach the treasure.

stages.title: Bargaining with the House
stages.clues: They deal with House Tremere over the devices and secrets: see The Secrets of Coeris.

neighbours.name: The Secrets of Coeris
neighbours.summary: House Tremere holds the laboratory, its texts and its devices to be its own, made for it with its resources; only the vis it leaves out of the claim. Getting them back matters far less to it than keeping its designs and triggering action secret.

stages.title: The House hears
stages.clues: Ferox or Fidelius tells it; a Tremere who knows the defenses spots or hears of a text or device; or the characters let it slip.

stages.title: Negotiation
stages.clues: Legal argument over ownership, with tempting offers of books and vis. No threat of immediate Wizard's War, for fear frightened magi publish.
stages.ignored: The House makes life extremely hard for them until they deal, keeping the means vague; Wizard's War is implied only if they spread the secrets.
stages.stopped: It pays any reasonable price, which can be high, but must rebuild Coeris's defenses anyway and buys time rather than trust.

stages.title: Forgetting and testimony
stages.clues: It wants the triggering action gone from unwanted minds, by Scraping Razor of Memory, spontaneous and perhaps non-fatiguing with Ceremonial Casting (Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 59). Before paying it asks each party to testify to a Tremere Mentem expert or a neutral Quaesitor, under Frosty Breath of the Spoken Lie or Ear of Truth (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 73), with checks for tampering such as Sight of the Active Magics. It must be voluntary, and the House will submit to like questions to prove its intent. It will ask if they know the secret, planned to recover it, know who else has it, and how they would have cheated.
stages.stopped: If all pass, the House thinks it has time to overhaul the defenses with care, and keeps its bargain.

neighbours.name: Trojan Clothes Horse
neighbours.summary: The characters find something once a Tremere magus's, perhaps robes. The House would like the finder to bring it to Coeris and tell how it was found, for a reward that barely pays the trip.

details.antagonist: A summoned spirit or creature of might

neighbours.secrets:
The item holds a Waiting Spell, perhaps hidden by Masking the Odor of Magic, that wakes inside Coeris and summons a strong being bent on all the harm it can do. It appears among the characters, who may not be taken for bystanders. They, it and the defenders chase one another through the sentinels and justiciars.

Outside the vaults these devices are built to delay, hold and above all raise the alarm, and several in Coeris locate any that fire. A raid on the vaults themselves is no fit story: the defenses, the House's resolve and the Order all stand against it (p. 98).

neighbours.name: Unexpected Copies
neighbours.summary: A magus has found a Vestige in the Magical Realm very like Coeris, and roughly set down how he reached it. The characters may retrace his way, to see if it holds like riches or like inhabitants.

neighbours.name: Dispatched
neighbours.summary: The House may arm its magi from these devices at need, so the characters can meet them away from Coeris. A Tremere maga with mundane helpers has gone into a regio for vis, nearer the characters' covenant than any other, and roused its inhabitants (fire spirits, demons, great clever spiders, as suits the saga). Defending her people she fell into Twilight. Her familiar escapes to the covenant to beg for rescue.
neighbours.secrets: The rescuers face both the inhabitants and the maze of sentinels and justiciars the trapped party has set up to protect itself.

neighbours.name: The Wreck of Thomae's Castle
neighbours.summary: A castle of bronze lies broken on the side of a snowy peak, its courtyard a single bronze sheet, its finials cast as dogs, its bells hanging silent from their chains. The foot of the High Tower is torn open by huge claws.
neighbours.secrets:
Where it is: the book sets the crash in the Alps, on a peak beyond a range of mountains about half a day west of Santa Lucia, and leaves the place to the saga. Skilled questioning of the villagers (Presence with Leadership or Charm, Ease Factor 12) gives a closer position. No aura is printed. How badly it is damaged is the storyguide's. Mended or altered a little, it can be the start of a Spring covenant (p. 121). The griffon alternatives story offers other reasons it fell. The bodies of Santa Lucians killed on the road lie heaped in the courtyard, their ghosts penned there by the Dogs of the Castle.

The griffons' claw marks: Intelligence + Magic Lore against 18 shows a giant eagle made them, 12 if the site has been scoured for mixed giant eagle feathers and lion hairs. A griffon may be glimpsed far off (Perception + Awareness 18). A ghost or a befriended faerie hound may tell.

The Flight Disk (p. 123): a single flat circle of hard stone 300 paces across and just under a pace thick, in a metal jacket beneath the bronze courtyard: a lesser enchanted device, not Hermetic Architecture, of one season's work. ReTe level 33, Pen +0, constant. R: Personal, D: Diameter, T: Individual. Flies the castle at a horse's running speed, steered by colored lights. It triggers itself whenever the spell is not running, so a single PeVi cannot bring it down and the flight never jerks. Base 3, +1 Diameter, +3 size, +1 stone; unlimited use +10, environmental trigger +3.

The Control Chain (p. 123): a steel chain fixed to the disk's center, rising through the High Tower to the laboratory, ending in a metal bulb. Doors in its tube let it be reached from many rooms. Touch it and speak Latin commands, and the bulb shines in colors and strengths that steer the disk. CrIg level 9, Pen +0, constant. R: Personal, D: Sun, T: Individual. Base 1, +2 Sun, +2 caster's control of color; constant use +4. It has many spare patterns, called by speaking numbers, meant for later additions to the disk. This is what killed him: the griffon's hole cracked the jacket, sunlight fell on the disk, and the castle listed before he could work out why. A separate item from the disk.

Boundary effects (p. 123): they do not move, so an Aegis of the Hearth or Boundary ward on the castle would be left behind as it flew. That is why it has no Aegis. Thomae trusted its reputation and his soldiers.

Laboratory notes (pp. 123-124): his laboratory was wrecked, but his best books survive in magical storage chests. The codices have lab notes for: the flying disk; the large laboratory it was made in; the control chain (useful for triggering other items from afar, in mines or under water); the siege finials, plain mystical artillery that look like all the other finials on the walls; Thomae's anchor, a whimsical ship's anchor trailed through the air behind and below the castle that hides the castle from the ground but not itself, bought or made after his legal troubles; Thomae's whip, his talisman, a long bronze chain that moves by magic, used to work things at a distance, extend Touch range and lash in battle; the falling bells; and the medallions of flight, invisibility, safe falling, attack and espionage. No levels are printed for these, and the book says only that the notes survive, not where the items lie.

The falling bells (p. 124): large bells in public spaces, whose sound the castle's bronze carried far. While in free fall they chime, and all who hear can fly for the rest of the day. Special winches let out one loop of chain at a time, so a bell drops a second before the slack takes it. These were for emergencies.

Training bell (p. 124): smaller bells for training, festivities and missions; servants learned to leap to a tower top and back, some to fly in earnest. ReCo level 35, Pen +0. R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Individual. Worked by holding the handle and ringing. The user flies at a brisk walk for the rest of the day. Tapped on a child as it rings it gives guided flight, and in theory it could be swung as a club to set a victim flying. Base 10, +1 Touch, +2 Sun; constant use +10.

Thomae's tender (pp. 124-125): a floating metal platform for lifting stores, faster than the castle, able to scout ahead or catch up. It was meant as expedition vehicle and lifeboat but never so used, and lacks climate control, artillery or incorrupt food stores. A large moonstone powers it: moved to a like metal plate, it powers that one. Its words are plain Latin, found by patient trial, in the ruins, or in the laboratory. ReTe level 34, Pen +0, constant. R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Individual. Carries as much as can be piled on it. Base 3, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +2 size, +2 metal; constant use +4.

If the characters cannot fly, a medallion, the tender or a training bell may turn up here to bring the griffons' lair within reach (p. 133).

Covenant goods (p. 125): a laboratory, a private library, and stores to keep his servants in luxury, much destroyed by the crash and the weather since. Not enough to equip a covenant's laboratories, but there may be enchanted lab equipment, valuable books, or wealth to buy supplies. Storyguides may place items from the book's other chapters here.

The bronze (p. 125): he chose it because a skin of corrosion stops its decay. It sells at 200 to 300 Mythic Pounds a ton, or up to 1,500 reworked as fine brassware. The trouble is weight, remoteness and flooding the market, not supply.

The griffons attack anything flying larger than a bird, horses and draft animals, and gold-carriers. See Flights of Fancy.

neighbours.name: Santa Lucia
neighbours.summary: A tiny mountain village of folk who speak a rough, homely Latin and are ruled by three councilors with metal badges of office. Its pasture has grown too poor for its growing numbers, and the village is packing up to move before winter.
neighbours.secrets:
The book places it in the Alps and tells the storyguide to change its name and place to suit the saga. Its people are the castle's surviving covenfolk and their children. Many of the old ones have skills of use to magi, learned aboard, and a covenant short of skilled folk could recruit them (p. 126).

Their folk tale (p. 131): they served a wizard, Thomae, with a castle in the sky, which 'bird-cats' destroyed. He had made sure that his servants could fly a little if it fell, and they escaped into the eye of the sun, where the monsters could not follow. Intelligence + Magic Lore 12 shows the bird-cats to be griffons.

The three badges were the marks of Thomae's bodyguards. Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore 12 recognizes them (21 normally, lowered because the characters are looking for just this and hold a twin). If it suits, they are magical, and may pass some of Thomae's defenses. The book names one councilor, Rogerio. They are the last symbolic tie to the castle (see Flights of Fancy).

neighbours.name: The New Valley of Santa Lucia
neighbours.summary: A valley the Santa Lucians are making their own, with carts on the road, temporary bridges and fords, and a village still to build.
neighbours.secrets: An allod: land no nobleman claims, which makes a fine site for a Spring covenant, with the castle and the Santa Lucians as the saga's first story (p. 126). In that case the griffons are likely too much for newly Gauntleted magi, and one of the griffon alternatives should take their place. Its location is left to the saga. Santa Lucia's work there is in Flights of Fancy.

neighbours.name: The Griffons' Nest of Gold
neighbours.summary: A nest high in some place no man can climb to, woven of gold, griffon feathers and the woods of strange trees, with eggs like great polished agates.
neighbours.secrets:
Griffons lair where few can reach. The book gives no place, only that its range overlaps the crash site. Ways of finding it are in Flights of Fancy.

The Nest of Gold (p. 125): a fortune in gold, and worth more as a focus: +7 to enchantments for defending a home or protecting treasure. To use it, it must reach a laboratory with its structure whole, by careful handling, skilled goldsmithing to solder it, or magic, until it can be stabilized and enchanted. An intact nest may also be needed for eggs to hatch.

Eggs of Agate (p. 125): griffon eggs are flawless agates the size of an ostrich's. Agate in the mouth is said to stop thirst, and sorcerers have used it since Rome to rule rivers and storms. Linked to Auram magic (+3), protection from storms (+5), and protection from venom (+7). Shells of hatched eggs may be enchanted the same way.

Baby griffons (pp. 125-126): hatched at a covenant they grow slowly, little bigger than dogs for decades, and do as they are told if they accept someone local as head of their pride. They act like flying kittens with keen sight and the strength to tear holes in things, and may suit as familiars. Magic can hasten their growth, but grown griffons are far harder to train, being notoriously impossible to coerce. Rules for training magical animals are in Realms of Power: Magic p. 81.

Griffons prey on livestock and would ruin farming, so they belong in far mountains. The Avars' flight west in the sixth century is sometimes laid to a plague of them (p. 130).

neighbours.name: Thomae's Secret Laboratory
neighbours.summary: A workshop no one has found, built to make the greatest enchantment the Order has seen.
neighbours.secrets: Thomae set it up to make the disk, and his Verditius collaborator has kept it (p. 138). Where it is, the book leaves open; one suggestion puts it in a small African or Asian kingdom Thomae conquered. His lab notes for it survive in the wreck. Its stories are in Thomae's Secret: The Verditius.

neighbours.name: Flights of Fancy
neighbours.summary: An unseen thief is robbing a large town near the covenant, by a power that looks like the work of a magus.

details.antagonist: The griffons, and the Dogs of the Castle

stages.title: Foreshadowing
stages.clues: In earlier stories, let Thomae pass by in a word: art of his castle, a mention in a legal case. Let griffons be seen too: a covenant's old archmage's staff tipped with an ostrich-egg agate a griffon laid, griffons as decoration in art.

stages.title: The Hidden Thief
stages.clues: Crimes by an invisible man in a large town near the covenant. Reasons to care: magically aided crime gets blamed on magi; the thief may be a magus, and a public worry a Hermetic crime; a charm means a magus made it, too near the covenant; such items often come from murdered redcaps; a robbed man or his servants ask for help or justice; the covenant's trade is hit.

stages.title: To Catch the Thief
stages.clues: Get to a burgled site by bribes, social rolls, magic or housebreaking. Awareness 6: the thief flew, for the roof shows no tool or foot marks. A second roll: he was looking for what he could find, not one thing. Catch him by Arcane Connections at the site, by criminal contacts tracing the goods, or by a pattern in the robberies that sets a trap.

stages.title: Recognizing the Link
stages.clues: The medal, held by Andros. Order of Hermes Lore 3: the spiral is House Tytalus's. Order of Hermes Lore 9 ties it to Thomae's legend, +3 for knowing the prayer to Saint Thomas, +3 for Hermetic Architects. Intelligence + Magic Theory 3: Verditius runes and a personal mark at the bottom edge. Order of Hermes Lore 15 knows the mark, 12 noting the onion sigil; House Verditius Lore 6, or 3. Redcaps and hoplites can name the magus, perhaps for a big favor. A player who sees it needs no roll.

stages.title: Following the Lead
stages.clues: To Santa Lucia, by: Roberto's belongings; his ghost; other Santa Lucian lads soldiering in a nearby war, as guides; a redcap who knows; or Flavia of Verditius and her Arcane Connection to Thomae.

stages.title: The Road
stages.clues: An isolated, slow journey carrying what could normally be bought on the way. Give spotlight to those not yet used. Monsters: the Elemental Blizzard, the Despair Demon. Environmental puzzles for spontaneous casters and non-fighters: a fallen rope bridge over a ravine; a path under unstable snow where noise brings avalanches; a river swollen by early melt; long travel above the snowline; a blizzard needing shelter or diverting.

stages.title: The Santa Lucians
stages.clues: The villagers race winter to shift goods and cattle to new pasture. Solve their problems for their help finding the castle: dig a well three feet wide and 30 deep; clear or pave main roads; replace temporary bridges and fords; raise chapel, mill, granary, calving sheds, bakery and smokehouse; clear land for orchards and fields; fence pasture; cut hay; slaughter and preserve beasts that cannot winter. Their tales place the castle half a day west, with no roll.

stages.title: The Dogs of the Castle
stages.clues: Bronze dogs attack parties hauling goods to the new site. Destroy them, or question them with Intellego Mentem. The cause shows only to one who can read glamor, or who sees the guarded heap of bodies at the wreck and makes Intelligence + Faerie Lore 6. Faerie Lore 15 shows that castle trinkets matter. A faerie may be tracked home.
stages.ignored: They go on killing the movers and penning their ghosts at the castle.
stages.stopped: Fight them, at the cost of more attacks if the tie remains.
stages.turned: If the leaders give up Thomae's badges and make new symbols for the village, the last link is cut, and the faeries lose interest. A hound attached to the characters' story may guide them, even to the griffons, to see a great battle.

stages.title: The Crash Site
stages.clues: Claws holed the highest tower. Learning griffons did it: claw marks; a ghost; a hound; a griffon sighted; or a flock of juvenile females snatching horses, mules, donkeys or unwarded gold and fleeing, not fighting to the death.
stages.turned: Sneakery, played as an environmental puzzle: work the wreck unnoticed by tunnels, by hiding the scent of draft animals, by flying invisibly, or whatever fits the Arts. No fight is needed, while repairing or salvaging.

stages.title: The Lair of the Griffons
stages.clues: Only needed for the nest of gold, or if subtlety fails. Finding it: horsemeat as bait (Intelligence + Artes Liberales 12 recalls how Alexander trapped four griffons with it and drove them through the air with carcasses dangling before them), with an Arcane Connection kept to the meat until a chick is fed; Intellego Animal on feathers or hairs from the wreck, which must beat Magic Resistance; a faerie who wants to witness the battle; or following a beaten flock home.
stages.stopped: Combat with the griffons, adult female and male (one of each at most), juveniles and hatchlings.
stages.turned: The nest, eggs and young become the troupe's.

neighbours.secrets: The adventure of the chapter (pp. 126-133). The thief's medal leads to a mountain village, its bronze hounds, and the wreck of Thomae's castle. The Dogs and griffons need not be fought: each has a subtler answer below. Griffons attack gold-carriers, draft animals (horses above all, which they love) and anything flying bigger than a bird.

neighbours.name: Hatching the Griffons' Eggs
neighbours.summary: Agate eggs from the nest of gold lie cold. No magus knows how they hatch, or even if they die away from their nest.
neighbours.secrets: Story seed (p. 125). It may take a story to find a way: a favor to the covenant with a great library; a powerful Bjornaer said to take griffon shape; Jerbiton covenants that train magical beasts, and a maga at remote Valnastium with potent items for training griffons, who may never have hatched one and may be too far to reach in time. It is unknown whether eggs die outside the right environment or wait for their mystic climate.

neighbours.name: Griffon Alternatives
neighbours.summary: What if something other than griffons brought down the castle? It may be waiting for the next who tries to fly.

details.antagonist: A demon of Pride, or a flock of magical moths

neighbours.secrets:
Alternatives to the griffons (p. 137), which the book also suggests for a saga's first story (p. 126).

A demon: a powerful one of an Order that punishes human sin struck the castle down, taking flight as Pride. The castle mends with little trouble, and the mender becomes its target. It may be mixed with the griffons to give the covenant a new Enemy. The book gives no statistics.

Moths: a flock of ethereal magical moths flew through the side of the disk to the light within. Set the chain's orb to black and offer another mystic light, with simple CrIm or CrIg spells of Ring duration, to lure them out of the works.

neighbours.name: Griffons in Other Tales
neighbours.summary: Griffons guard more than a golden nest: old Greek tales set them at the edges of the world and beside the gods' arms.
neighbours.secrets:
Ties to earlier books (p. 137). Aristeas's lost Arimaspea, reported by Herodotus, sets griffons close to the north wind, their land dividing Hyperborea from the world. Magi after Hyperborean magic (Ancient Magic) could tame one and use its migratory sense to seek the land of gold.

Aristeas was a Nightwalker. In Hedge Magic's story a faerie Aristeas tries to turn the cult from the Lady to Apollo, and is said to have hidden his body in the griffons' land.

In the Hesperides quest (Ancient Magic), one outcome seeks the weapons of the old gods. A Greek poem gives Zeus griffons as guard dogs, so they may nest on the mountain hiding the Titans' weapons.

neighbours.name: Thomae's Secret: The Verditius
neighbours.summary: Thomae had a Verditius helper who has never claimed the credit. Why would a Verditius stay so modest?
neighbours.secrets: What Thomae was hiding is the troupe's to choose (p. 138). Point to it with: who or what was his 'Verditius collaborator', and where is his ghost? The Verditius has kept the secret laboratory and hides it for a reason: it holds prohibited faerie or demonic elements; or it lies at the heart of a small African or Asian kingdom Thomae conquered, probably against the Code; or it has spent twenty years turning out flying squares that clip together into a platform for a flying city.

neighbours.name: Thomae's Secret: Faerie Dealings
neighbours.summary: Time and money should have stopped Thomae. Something else paid, and may yet come for the debt.
neighbours.secrets: What Thomae was hiding is the troupe's to choose (p. 138). Point to it with: who or what was his 'Verditius collaborator', and where is his ghost? He built the castle and items in Arcadia, solving both limits. If he died there unknowing, what came back was a powerful faerie, which is why there is no ghost and why creatures perfect for his story struck him down; his wanderings to far mountains may have been his glamor seeking to finish its script. Faeries trade wishes for vitality, and so large a thing brought out of Faerie means vast vitality given, or promised. A collector comes, or takes the castle back: a dark faerie wanting the blood of the dead of a war he promised to start, or a Queen of Sylphs demanding the tears of ten thousand babies, this century's rent for her flying throne.

neighbours.name: Thomae's Secret: The Found Object
neighbours.summary: The control chain is plainly Hermetic. The great disk may be something far older.
neighbours.secrets: What Thomae was hiding is the troupe's to choose (p. 138). Point to it with: who or what was his 'Verditius collaborator', and where is his ghost? Herodotus tells of Chemiss, a floating island bearing a temple of Apollo. Hunting vis in Egypt, Thomae found that a stone disc held it up, worked out, perhaps with help, that colored lights steered it, and spent his missing years ordering the lesser items. His Verditius ally lets others think he built it, keeping the bragging rights, and exposure would wound his standing. In myth, Latona or a priestess made the island float to hide Apollo (Horus) from Typhon (Set); she was the city goddess of Buto, with an oracle there by Herodotus, so some trace may remain. So the disc hid a faerie from a magical being in Egypt's Titanomachy. What else lay beneath it: a weapons cache's capstone, a faerie road's door? What goes on there now he has taken this barrier away?

characters.name: Conciatta of Bonisagus
characters.summary:
Born Dolorita, a wealthy merchant's daughter of Barcelona, about 885. Baltasar of Bonisagus took her to Leon and fostered her out as far as Al Andalus, Provence and Lombardy, and she left apprenticeship hungry to reach the unseen realms by Hermetic means alone. She worked as a laboratory assistant across Iberia and beyond. On her travels she met Currito of Jerbiton, and within a year they had raised a tower in a regio at Zaragoza and married.

Her peers held that the realms would yield only to new Arts. She disagreed, and in 930 published The Application of Vim to the Supernatural Humors (tractatus on Magic Theory, quality 7), showing that auras fall into four categories matching the realms and that Vim can reach all four. Her name was made. Then Baltasar confessed to Infernal corruption and was marched; her rivals used it, her sex and her youth against her, and she was quietly shut out of Bonisagus society. She sent her last unfinished notes to Durenmar.

For forty years she studied strange places and published nothing, while Currito found her vis and books. In the end he left, and she stayed on alone in her tower while the world forgot her. The Order holds that she vanished into Twilight before the millennium. Her fame survives as a primer and, among Bonisagi, a warning.

Vim itself, as the Founders taught it, covered only active magic; the Forms did what Vim now does (p. 15). Much of the language magi use of auras is hers: diffuse and tethered; stable, waning and waxing; existential and moral; apparent and subsumed.
characters.secrets:
Her Gift grew blatant and magic began to leak from her unbidden, ruining her studies and drawing Twilight on. After five years alone, as the millennium turned, she went to a convent near Toledo she knew from her research, hoping the Dominion would quiet it. It did for a while. Warping took her into Final Twilight eleven years on, and her spirit broke into four aspects, one for each realm, which fled the convent. Each keeps something of her and guards a part of her unpublished breakthroughs (p. 14).

What the Order Remembers (p. 14; rule pp. 10-11): Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore simple roll; the character recalls everything up to the Ease Factor reached. Bonisagi add +3, for her rank of Cannophori (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 21). Research in a fit library: Covenants p. 98.
Ease Factor 0, Known by All: she brought the four realms under the single Art of Vim; apprentices often study her The Application of Vim to the Supernatural Humors; she left Hermetic society in later life.
Ease Factor 6, Widely Known: she lived in Iberia, with ties to Christian and Muslim communities alike; her parens was marched for diabolic corruption; her husband, a Jerbiton artist, aided her work.
Ease Factor 12, Uncommon Knowledge: some hold she kept part of her research from the Order; she overcame the Dominion's effect on magic (false: a distortion grown from Currito's later writings); she vanished into Twilight before the turn of the millennium (what the Order at large believes, and false).
Ease Factor 18, Lost Secrets: the hubris of her research cost her control of her magic; she died in a convent near Toledo; shortly before her death four women came to her, and she gave each a magical treasure.

List of Artifacts (p. 18), with integration or breakthrough points:
Confluence of the Realms: Maintaining the Unstable Conjuration 6, The Fourfold Lens 11, Subsume the Apparent Dominion 10.
Insight of the Realms: Clearing the Mind of the Caster 6, The Insightful Stylus 5, The Lodestone 7, The Sands of Time 4.
True Understanding of the Realms: Ward Against Woodland Spirits 9.
The table calls the first Maintaining the Divine Conjuration; p. 30 prints it as Maintaining the Unstable Conjuration.

Her new Virtues and Flaw, spells and guidelines (pp. 14-18) are in the catalogs: Confluence, Insight and True Understanding of the Realms; The Constant Expression, which magi Initiating her Virtues take through ordeal; To See What Binds this Magical Place; This Heart of Darkness; Dominance Over the Infernal. Her guidelines may be used by any maga who has studied one of her unpublished works. Integrating her discoveries: Ancient Magic p. 7; original research: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 26; summary: Hedge Magic Revised Edition p. 14; the two add together (p. 18). The book gives her dates as c. 885 to 1007, yet has her at the convent eleven years from the new millennium (p. 14).

characters.name: Currito of Jerbiton
characters.summary:
An artist at heart and Conciatta's husband, impetuous and confident. He found the auras of Zaragoza and founded La Torre no Vista with her. His paintings were mostly religious, though for a time rich covenants prized his Hermetic triptychs, and frescoes of his can still be found across the Order.

He gave up his own studies and art to supply his wife, was mocked by his peers for it, and after she went a full year without seeing him he left Zaragoza, bitter, with some of her notes to sell. Reports put him in the Levant before 1000. By the Schism War his best days were long gone, and he ended as a wandering artist living on old fame and old friends' hospitality until his welcome wore out. In unguarded moments he spoke of a great prize: Hermetic magic fueled by the Dominion's own aura.
characters.secrets:
The Life of Currito (p. 22): his book, written in age, in a shaky hand between leather flaps; a five-day distraction to read. It tells that their hidden covenant was still plagued by birds from the mundane world; that Conciatta stayed in Zaragoza after La Torre no Vista dissolved; that she studied the Dominion at a convent in Toledo and ended her days there; that they survived an Infernal cave system at Narixa and left notes and a map in the library of the al Narixa mosque; and, with evident bitterness and no detail, that she bargained for knowledge with the king of a lost city outside Qadis, which began to turn her from him.

A full-page illumination shows her under a wide arch, its pillars held up on one side by an angel on a demon, on the other by a dragon on a winged man with a lute. Hermetic text fills the wall behind her: the missing part of the cellar's casting tablet.

Books and devices he took may turn up in a covenant's library or stores, and casting tablets of his on auras too; his surviving frescoes can foreshadow the story by showing one subject as touched by the four realms (p. 19).

characters.name: Reyes de Barbastro

description.biography:
A big man fond of too much food and drink, round and ruddy in the face, his black hair thinning. He dresses to show what he is worth, as a man of his standing should. Merchant clothing.

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense +0; fist Init -1, Attack +1, Defense +0, Damage +0; bludgeon Init -2, Attack +4, Defense +1, Damage +2. Soak 0. Fatigue OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Capo, Many Marriageable Daughters and Vernacular Education are from City & Guild pp. 108-109; the catalog has the last as Educated (Vernacular). His Weakness is Hedonism. LoH p. 24.

characters.summary: A prosperous Zaragoza merchant whose home and warehouse look over the Ebro. He trades chiefly in wine from Logroño, where he keeps another warehouse, but will buy and sell most things. He has three daughters, of 17, 16 and 14, and no sons, and wants husbands who will care for his business and his daughters, in that order.
characters.secrets: His warehouse cellar bounds the old covenant's aura, which he knows nothing of. Characters wanting the cellar may appeal to his wish for sons-in-law (pp. 23-24).

characters.name: Abbess Prudencia

description.biography:
She strides about her convent with complete authority and a withering look, straight of neck and back, eyebrows raised, hands clasped, her eyes always finding some fault. Two novices follow her and do as she bids.

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense -1; fist Init -1, Attack +0, Defense -1, Damage -1. Soak +1. Fatigue OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Magic Resistance 10, from her relic. Clear Thinker gives +3 to resist lies, confusion and subterfuge. Senior Clergy is from Realms of Power: The Divine p. 93. LoH p. 29.

reputations.name: Abbess of a convent in need of money (Toledo)

characters.summary: Abbess of the Convento de San Ildefonso, thought strict and aloof; the aloofness is mostly contempt for the men who come to her convent for their own secular gain. She knows little of magic and dislikes magi at her door.
characters.secrets:
She unknowingly wears a relic of San Ildefonso, a cord from his robe wound into a belt handed from abbess to abbess, with one Faith Point. She holds the vow, passed down the line of abbesses, to protect the spirit, and will not lightly break it (pp. 29-30).

Winning her trust: a task she needs done, of no great danger, that lets the characters show virtue; a good name for kindness, charity or judgment around Toledo; or generosity to the convent. If she is persuaded the spirit harms the girl, she will not let the suffering go on, and lets the magi try to part them (p. 32).

characters.name: Novice Immaculada

description.biography:
A small girl of seventeen, pale and tear-streaked, her eyes red with crying. Her hair is shorn and her habit has given way to a dirty white smock and cap; her nails are picked and bitten raw. Chalk covers her fingers, face and clothes.

Combat: dodge Init +0, Defense +0; fist Init +0, Attack +2, Defense +0, Damage +0. Soak 0. Fatigue OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

Confidence: none. Enfeebled and Visions are imposed by the spirit within her; the rest of the block is the girl as she should be. She rarely sleeps, so is always at a -3 Fatigue penalty. Her Warping is Divine. LoH p. 31.

characters.summary: The novice of the Convento de San Ildefonso whose visions the wealthy pay to hear. The sisters care for her, for she cannot care for herself. She lives in a windowless room lit by candles, among bedding, slates and parchment, writing and speaking in tongues without warning.
characters.secrets:
She carries the Divine Conciatta, the latest of generations of possessed novices, and fares worst of them all. The convent has long taken this for God's miracle, and its magical origin is all but forgotten (p. 29).

When visitors enter, sense surfaces in her babble (pp. 31-32): she once had many brothers and sisters and now only three, who hide, though she remembers where she went; Seiffeddin, an actor in Qadis, may know her and where she is; she would like to see her sisters.

Her fear of being alone binds the spirit to her. If that is abated, the spirit can pass to another host; how is left to the troupe (p. 32).

characters.name: Habib al-Hadi

description.biography:
A small wiry man, gray of hair and beard, with a large nose and a brow creased by thought and worry. His clothes are threadbare, since what money he has goes on his studies. He carries slates and chalk, quill, ink and parchment.

Combat: dodge Init -1, Defense -1; fist Init -1, Attack -1, Defense -1, Damage -2; bludgeon Init -2, Attack +1, Defense -1, Damage +0. Soak -1. Fatigue OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

'Alim is from Realms of Power: The Divine p. 114. The block spells his Area Lore Cadis Lore; the same city. LoH p. 34.

characters.summary: A scholar of Qadis, and cleric, astronomer, translator and teacher, who takes any work that keeps him in food and parchment, though not always in that order. He can be met at night searching the city with a strange instrument, and likes nothing better than to talk to the learned. His observatory is his room on the top floor of a tenement in a poor and noisy district.
characters.secrets:
He found the Fourfold Lens lately, took it for a device to study the heavens, and has seen auras and the ghostly citizens through it. He files what he sees under the four elements, tying them uncertainly to the four auras. He is slow to lend or sell it, but may part with it if his study of supernatural Qadis can be fed some other way (pp. 34-35).

The Fourfold Lens (p. 34): an adjustable iron stand with four hand-sized lenses on swinging arms, each enchanted for one realm and clear if its aura is absent. Conciatta made it for her custos and Currito to take on journeys, and it was lost on one. Each lens is Unveil the Subsumed (Realm), InVi 54, constant (R Personal, D Sun, T Vision, 2/day triggered at sunrise and sunset): it shows any aura present of its realm, subsumed or not, and the world as that aura would make it. It finds subsumed auras of any level but can only penetrate an apparent aura of level 3, and only the lowest level of each, so it does not show regiones. Re-creating it gives 11 points toward Confluence of the Realms.

characters.name: Imam Hamid ibn Harun

description.biography:
A small aging man with a gray beard, eyes narrowed from squinting and a toothless smile. Dust seems to find his turban and robes, and his library has plenty to spare.

Combat: fist Init -2, Attack +0, Defense +0, Damage -1. Soak 0. Fatigue OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wound penalties: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

'Alim, Islamic Law and Theology: Islam are from Realms of Power: The Divine. LoH p. 40.

characters.summary: An imam of the Al Narixa Mosque all his adult life, kept mostly to its library. He suffers visions he takes for warnings from Allah, always of tunnels, caves, and hungry yellow eyes in the dark.
characters.secrets: If the caves are spoken of with or near him in Arabic, he also sees a seductive queen clothed in smoke and fire (p. 40).

characters.name: Fortunata of Jerbiton
characters.summary:
Lived 986 to about 1123. Daughter of a prince of Milan, she was taken as apprentice around 996 by Apollo of Jerbiton, who saw her Gentle Gift. Her childhood name is lost; she took the name Fortunata at her Gauntlet. She became a fine scholar and made her parens proud, but envied the potent specialised magic of others and came to want it more than the learning of her House.

As a young maga of the Rome Tribunal she travelled the old Roman and Greek ruins around the Mediterranean. She freed a spirit, Lucida, from a witch's binding in a cleft stone, and they became friends, travelling companions, and in time maga and familiar; some said lovers.

She pursued the rites of lost cults. Her sudden power led rivals to accuse her of dealing with demons and of spying through spirits. The charges dogged her, and her secrecy did not help, so in later years she quit her covenant for a hidden island, keeping a house in Venice for the Redcaps. Those who met her reported shimmering clouds of spirits around her.

She translated dead languages by having ancient ghosts read texts aloud while Mentem magic let her understand them, and many of her Latin versions spread through the Order, with notes in the margins that leave a reader wanting the rest. She was last met in 1123.
characters.secrets:
She dealt with no demons: she mastered Self-Initiation, turning quests into power with no cult to obey, and named the system Principles Lore (p. 47). She was careful of the Quaesitores and did not use her spirits to spy. She probably died or entered Final Twilight soon after 1123; the chapter's heading says Final Twilight, its text that her fate is not recorded. Her island and library wait to be opened.

She claimed to have found these rites in the ancients, yet many are Hermetic Virtues and there was no Hermetic magic before Bonisagus. She may have been deluded, may have lied, or may have had a knack for scripts that closely paralleled ancient Virtues (p. 47). The book leaves it open.

She never learned the ancient tongues, only called spirits until one could read the text (p. 68).

What the Order Remembers (p. 48): a simple roll of Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore recalls everything up to the Ease Factor it reaches (p. 10). Some of it is false, grown from envy and from the fable she has become. A library can be searched as well (Covenants p. 98).
Known by All (Ease Factor 0):
- A spirit master and maga of House Jerbiton.
- Active in the Rome Tribunal, she left it for a private retreat.
- She beat many enemies outside the Order in southern Europe and North Africa.
- Her power came from ancient lore, and she translated the ancients.
- She robbed many Mysteries of their power.
- Her books are said to tell how to win the same powers.
- Hermetic enemies drove her into exile.
- She vanished into Twilight about 1123.
Widely Known (Ease Factor 6):
- She kept no familiar, only a spirit who went with her.
- A cloud of airy spirits surrounded her, quick to obey.
- [Jerbiton magi only] A very gifted scholar who failed her House through envy of magical power.
- She belonged to no known Mystery Cult, though she wrote of many.
- [Redcaps only] Her house in Venice welcomed Redcaps richly.
Uncommon Knowledge (Ease Factor 12):
- She answered charges of infernalism and magical spying and walked free, then retired anyway.
- She owned and ran a house in Venice, for years a meeting place of Redcaps.
- Her retreat lay among the many small islands of the Ionian Sea, or whichever part of the Mediterranean suits the saga.
- Many admired her scholarship, but her parens was disappointed.
- By magic she translated scrolls no one could read, going past the Hermetic limits on translation.
Lost Secrets (Ease Factor 18): the book lists none for her. It says a few details are known only to some Redcaps or Jerbiton magi, and gives no bonus to any House's roll.

characters.name: Cupressa of Algiers
characters.summary: Long dead. A witch banished from Algiers for her dark practices, who left carrying her beast-son Monocaudus and cursed the city with seven years of failed harvests. By black arts she bound the spirit Lucida and took an island in the Mediterranean, where she raised her son. She died of old age.
characters.secrets: Her tradition resembles the Witches of Thessaly (Realms of Power: The Infernal p. 140) and still reveres her (p. 57). Monocaudus's tale that Fortunata slew her is false (p. 64). The father of her son was Omaion the Serpent.

characters.name: Omaion the Serpent
characters.summary: A great magical snake some 30 feet long, with penetrating venom and leathery skin that turns any weapon, who can also walk as a beautiful, lithe and seductive man. He may wander far from his cave in that shape.
characters.secrets:
The father of Monocaudus, whom legend does not name (p. 58). He has hardly met a magus. The book gives him no stat block. See the story A Vengeful Father.

Legends differ, and a saga may choose another version. Omaion the Infernal: a demon in the shape of a jet-skinned handsome man, in a fortified mansion in the old quarter of Algiers among beautiful servants and apparent wealth, Monocaudus's beast form then being Infernal and Magical blood mixed in flesh. Omaion the Sorcerer: one of the darker fae of Greece, brooding in dark forest glades, with a dragon's head and tail, a lion's chest, a man's arms and a goat's nether parts; to imply his origin is such a mixture of myths risks instant wrath.

characters.name: Lucio
characters.summary: The ghost of an elderly servant in an old Venetian house, who stayed faithful long after his mistress disappeared, until a gruesome plague killed him around 1130. He means no harm, and talks in an old Venetian dialect to anyone who can see him and does not run: of old Venice, of the maga who came to work on her books and letters, and of how he died.
characters.secrets: He knows that Fortunata hid papers behind wall panels and under floorboards (p. 56). The book gives him no stat block.

characters.name: Chrétien the Roamer
characters.summary: A disreputable-looking monk, tall and forever tousled, who has wandered much of Europe, the southern Mediterranean coasts and England above all. A great storyteller, he has somehow survived many disasters and seen many wonders, and tells them for ale.
characters.secrets: He knows much Church Lore, Dominion Lore, Magic Lore and Area Lore of England and the Mediterranean, which should serve the story and not be a guide to everything (p. 57). The book gives no scores.

characters.name: Federo of Bonisagus
characters.summary: An elderly magus who has studied Fortunata's life and gathered a great deal about her. He is sure she was a witch of Thessaly, sodalis, rival and at last victor over Cupressa of Algiers, and he has plans for expeditions to Algiers, Thessaly and various Mediterranean islands.
characters.secrets: Much of what he has is distorted, and the witches have fed him false information (p. 57).

characters.name: Pullatus of Flambeau
characters.summary: A magus obsessed with Viea, Trianoma's sister, and with dragons. He believes Viea founded a lineage of her own on knowledge stolen from Bonisagus, and that the sisters dealt with dragons. His research into her ideas and magics keeps him at his laboratory, so he looks for others to go in his stead.
characters.secrets: He takes Cupressa's son for a half-dragon, and Cupressa and Viea for one woman, which would make the island the home of a near-Founder (pp. 57-58). The book says nothing to support this. Viea's story is in Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 6.

characters.name: Hérisson of Bjornaer
characters.summary:
c. 857-1002. A magus of Clan Arelie whose heartbeast was the urchin, or hedgehog, and whose sigil ran to spines and thorns; a copper urchin was his voting sigil. He left his apprenticeship in 881 in Normandy and was at first an unremarkable worker of Herbam and magical agriculture. His House feared that mankind was killing Magic as forests fell, and some talked of culling the people; he held that Magic was boundless and went off to a backwater of his Tribunal to prove it.

As the Order drifted toward the Schism he preached peace, offered his research to House Bonisagus and put his theories to convocations of House Diedne. Few believed he could grow vis. His House tired of him and distrusted his dealings; Gypaetus of Bjornaer accused him of betraying cult secrets and declared Wizard's War. Past a hundred years old and no fighter, he was dead within two days of the full moon. While the House sat out the Schism in its domus magna, the head of Clan Arelie studied his political writings, and by 1019 half the clans had declared for living alongside mankind: the Concordiarii, or Harmonists.

What the Order Remembers (Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore, simple roll; +1 for Bjornaer, +3 for Clan Arelie, the House's memory; a character recalls everything up to the Ease Factor reached, and some of it may be false; Introduction pp. 10-11).

Ease Factor 0, Known by All: a magus of the ninth and tenth centuries; he built a magical Garden overflowing with vis, never yet found.

Ease Factor 6, Widely Known: the Harmonists' founder, at least in name; a hedgehog heartbeast; he claimed he could grow all but limitless vis and was never taken seriously; he died in Wizard's War at the hands of his own House.

Ease Factor 12, Uncommon Knowledge: Gypaetus of Bjornaer slew him; he quarrelled with his House and Primus, and was accused of showing House secrets to House Diedne.
characters.secrets:
Ease Factor 18, Lost Secrets: he may descend from Myanar; some think his spirit lives on in his Garden; a copy of part of his research went to the Great Library at Durenmar.

He was a theorist of the first rank who completed a Major Breakthrough, Hermetic Viresculture, and a Minor one extending it to Lesser Enchantment Vis (pp. 72-76). He was working toward making Lesser Enchantment Vis, and on the vis in gems and metals, when he died. He never made the method general.

A Descendant of Myanar? (pp. 71-72) Tales give him Nature Mysteries like House Merinita's, and the Garden's sentient plants look like the work of Awakening Nature (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p. 104). He may come of a follower of Myanar who fled to House Bjornaer when Quendalon became Primus. Magi who know the Nature Mysteries may ask whether he took Guardian of Nature and became a genius loci, his death a staged way out of the Order. If so he may haunt the Garden as its spirit, and if he belonged to a hidden Bjornaer cult his heirs may keep it still. The book does not settle any of this.

characters.name: Gypaetus of Bjornaer
characters.summary: Died 1035. A veteran hunter of Marched magi, who accused Hérisson of betraying cult secrets to magi hostile to the Order, declared Wizard's War and killed him within two days of the full moon. He left a single filia, Variña, whose line ended with her.
characters.secrets: Hérisson's will left him the fruits of the research, by way of apology for the trouble of having to kill its discoverer. The copy buried in the field names him as heir; the notes themselves are not with it (p. 77).

characters.name: Tasso Agricola Areleins
characters.summary:
Eldest of the Sept of Hérisson and its Mystagogue, three generations from its founder, and a master of Terram. Black hair with a white stripe rising from each temple tells the badger he holds within. He goes in a peasant's smock, with a woven hat in the fields, and speaks like a peasant. Friendly and guileless, he is to be found working the land around his rural covenant, which stands apart from Order politics, and which he shares with one other of the sept. His aim is bigger harvests, so that fewer forests fall for fields.

Age 64, apparent age 46. Gentle Gift; Study Bonus, which pays him for his labor with soil and crops (p. 78).
characters.secrets: He holds a few of Hérisson's laboratory texts, out of order and in cipher. He has never made sense of them, and lets the characters copy them if they will share what they learn of his ancestor, since such news is status in his House. Richard Strabo has made a friend of him with gifts of farming spells and enchantments, and passes for a friend still; word of anyone asking after Hérisson soon reaches Strabo. The book prints no Characteristics or Arts for him.

characters.name: Erica of Bjornaer
characters.summary: Tasso's filia, a mole in her heartbeast, and a prominent voice in Hermetic politics for living alongside mundanes and the Church. She dwells at a covenant near his. Asked about Hérisson, she will likely send the enquirer to Tasso, the sept's leader and heir to its founder's texts (pp. 72, 78-79).

characters.name: Caerfloron
characters.summary: Founder of the covenant that bears his name, a magus Ex Miscellanea of nearly 150 years with a passion for Herbam. He and his filii keep apart from the Order, content with its protection and with their right to be left alone.
characters.secrets:
