He is close to Final Twilight and will not risk his strongest spells. He enchanted the gate that leads into the Garden's regio (p. 83). The book prints no block for him or his filii.

A Homunculus Wizard of Realms of Power: Faerie chapter 5: a manikin made of a Mandrake of Virtue from Hérisson's Garden is the source of the wizard's magic, gained on one visit at the start of the career. The tradition gives Greater Immunity (Deprivation), Faerie Magic and the Homunculus Wizard Flaw, and all share Disfigured: a green tinge to skin and hair. No wounds or Fatigue from want of food, drink or air, but Long Term Fatigue returns only with rest and sustenance; the body runs on the vegetative spirit woken by daylight. Not of House Merinita, so barred from its Inner Mysteries (p. 83).

characters.name: Radix
characters.summary: One of the four filii of Caerfloron, living in a hut against the walls of their walled garden, and like the others devoted to Herbam.

characters.name: Richard Strabo

invented_spells.name: Disguise of the New Visage
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Legends of Hermes.

invented_spells.name: Free the Striding Tree
invented_spells.description: From the stat block in Legends of Hermes.

description.biography:
A man who looks to be in his middle years, dark-haired and weathered by the sun, with a fixed, hungry glint in the eye that unsettles people. He goes in a green cloak and a broad hat and never lays down his staff. Strabo is a name borrowed from a celebrated gardening monk, whose first name he sometimes uses as the alias Walahfrid. Sigil: the smell of damp earth. Twilight scars: arms like twisted roots; fruit does not spoil near him; he goes bald in winter.

Combat: evasion Init 0, Attack n/a, Defense 0, Damage n/a. Soak +2. Fatigue OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wounds -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+). Teaching 2 has 5 more experience points. Puissant Magic Theory is starred in the block, with no note to say why.

Talisman: a twisted, gnarled staff of ivy with leaves carved from six woods. Attunements: +3 affect living wood (wood), +3 Creo Herbam (almond). It holds two effects.

The Nimble Vine, Cr(Re)He 35, Penetration 20, unlimited uses: a strong vine as supple as an arm, eight inches thick and up to 500 paces long, extending at a walking pace, that grips, fetches, strangles or wields a weapon at the wielder's word, on the wielder's Finesse in place of any Ability. It cannot be directed when the wielder cannot see its hand. (Base 1, +1 Touch, +1 Conc, +2 size, +1 requisite; +5 maintains concentration, +10 unlimited uses, +10 Penetration 20.)

The Thrusting Root, Cr(Re)He 28, Penetration 20, 6/day: a spear-like ram shoots from the staff at anyone within 15 paces, for +10 damage. A Medium or worse wound pins the target, who cannot move but may attack the root. It can also batter doors and walls, forcing a Stress Check (City & Guild p. 77). (Base 1, +2 Voice, +1 Conc, +1 size, +1 requisite; +5 maintains concentration, +3 6/day, +10 Penetration 20.)

Casting Scores as printed (* Minor Magical Focus, T talisman attunement): Disguise of the New Visage +26; Shape of the Creeping Ivy +38*; Conjure the Sturdy Vine +39*T; The Giant's Beanstalk +39*T; The Chokeweed Incantation +39*T; Trap of the Entwining Vines +39*T; Wall of Thorns +29T; The Envenomed Thorns +29T; Intuition of the Forest +23; Piercing Shaft of Wood +26; Transformation of the Thorny Staff +30; Coils of the Entangling Plants +24; Free the Crawling Vine +32*; Lord of the Trees +27T; The Treacherous Spear +24; Free the Striding Tree +27T.

Disguise of the New Visage is a Personal variant at level 10, not the general level 15. Free the Striding Tree is printed so here; the Definitive Edition's spell is Freeing the Striding Tree.

Presented as a magus of the Rhine, but any fitting character will serve, so long as he is no prominent figure of the characters' own Tribunal. Richard Caespuus of Durenmar (Guardians of the Forests p. 58) suits, if the troupe accepts that whoever fills the part will likely face a Wizard's March. Built to test young magi; make him older for seasoned ones. He is a spy in plant form and a harasser, not a duellist (pp. 80-81).

characters.summary: A researcher of House Bonisagus who won Acclaim young, then soured under the weight of it. Nothing of his has satisfied the House in over twenty years, and he has grown bitter and solitary, dropping hints of a secret project that will change Hermetic magic.
characters.secrets:
Every line he tried came to nothing, until he found Hérisson's notes in a forgotten archive of Durenmar's library. He means to find the rest and pass the whole off as his own, and has staked his name on it. Discovery would finish him in his House, and he is unhinged enough to break the Code to prevent it. He corresponds under several aliases with Herbam experts across Mythic Europe, mining them for ideas, and cultivates Tasso as his sentinel. He has not thought of the tomb of the slayer's filia. See The Search for Hérisson's Garden.

By trying to have a magus killed he breaks the Oath and forfeits the Code's protection (p. 83).

characters.name: Hermanus of Tremere
characters.summary:
c. 940 to 1098 (Final Twilight). The master strategist who gave more than eighty years to making Coeris, the domus magna of House Tremere, a safe storehouse for the House's treasure. Thirty-nine years past his apprenticeship when the Schism War began, he served as a master of auxiliaries, training and leading mundane soldiers. Twice he won by foreseeing the attack: his unit, warded beforehand, outlasted two Diedne magi and their beasts until help came, and he hunted down and slew Nuala of Diedne, fifteen years his elder. He had no Gentle Gift and little persuasion, yet his troops held; so the primus gave him the Adamant Rook Vexillation, a group of enchanters.

The House could not count on better magi than its foes, or on magics they did not know. Hermanus used what it did have, its cohesion, drawing in as much of its magi and resources as he could to build a network of devices through the covenant that found and held anyone acting against the Tremere. The more he built, the less he was content; his mind came to see only weakness. In 1070 the primus dissolved the vexillation, calling the work excessive, and others began to ask whether the vis had been well spent. For twenty-eight years more he kept at it alone, arguing, seeking the primacy, studying and enchanting.

In the autumn of 1098, three hours after a last quarrel with the primus, the top floor of his wing of Coeris vanished with him, most think in Final Twilight. The Abyssal Bearer Vexillation (Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p. 122) searched, and the Unbarred Gateway Vexillation searched until early 1104. His fame outside the House came later (see Velius of Tremere).

What the Order Remembers (pp. 10-11, 96). Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore simple roll; the character recalls everything up to the Ease Factor reached. Research in a library: Covenants p. 98.

Ease Factor 0, Known by All: His Final Twilight took away a whole part of Coeris. He was a Schism War veteran who oversaw defenses for the House's resources. He is famed for marshalling so much of the House to that end for decades. He found Diedne sympathizers in House Tremere, a cabal that destroyed him and made his laboratory vanish.

Ease Factor 6, Widely Known: At the end he enchanted his laboratory to move, so he could see the world from behind its wards, and left Coeris and the House for good. He went on strengthening Coeris for twenty-eight years after the vexillation ended, clashing ever more with the primus and senior magi, and sought the primacy to further it.

Ease Factor 12, Uncommon Knowledge: A vexillation hunted for him and the laboratory, and after four years found them beyond any Tremere method. He ended a great expert in Intellego, but was chosen for leadership; the greatest Adamant Rook works were made by magi in groups. Age made him ever more fearful, seeing attacks in everything, and he took to sending an enchanted human-sized doll out for vis in his stead. He died seeking vis from a Provencal town besieged by giant bats, and all record of the town save this has been destroyed by someone or something keeping it secret.

Ease Factor 18, Lost Secrets: Amarantha of Tremere went on searching after the vexillation reported and dissolved. She disappeared in 1110, without a trace.
characters.secrets:
False among the recollections (p. 96): the Diedne cabal; the laboratory enchanted to move; the Provencal town of giant bats. Much of his work may be known only inside House Tremere (p. 11).

By 1091 he saw the House would never give him the vis, and meant to find it himself; but his fears kept him in his laboratory, behind eight warded rings. So he enchanted one of the Coeris mannequins and sent it out under his control, through Opening the Intangible Tunnel, to look for vis. That autumn evening in 1098 it stood on the sea floor off the south coast of Crete, among the wrecks of Demetrios the Poliorketes' battle with Ptolemy, and he tried to bring the vis home with a Rego spell from a casting tablet. The casting failed terribly. He and his familiar were lost to Final Twilight; the laboratory and its structure went to the Terram province of the Twilight Void, tethered to the mannequin and the vis.

characters.name: Amarantha of Tremere
characters.summary: Died late in 1110. A member of the Unbarred Gateway Vexillation who would not let the search end when it dissolved in 1104. She questioned those who had spoken with Hermanus or his familiar, read what he had read in his last years, and went through their letters. By 1110 she had a long list of places he might have sent his mannequin, and set off alone to visit them, telling no one: she feared looking a fool, and doubting the vexillation would have offended influential magi of the House.
characters.secrets: Her end came far from help, somewhere the Abyssal Bearer Vexillation, charged with recovering the bodies of Tremere magi, never knew of. Her notes held some ideas for researching a spell to bring the laboratory back, but no firm plan. See The Remains of Amarantha.

characters.name: Velius of Tremere
characters.summary: Archmage from 1104; Final Twilight 1120. Come to Coeris from the Rhine Tribunal, he took on the danger of a vanished wing full of the covenant's own devices, shored up the defenses, then kept them working. In 1115 his former apprentice challenged him; he set her to fetch a token from a Coeris vault within the year, and she failed. Elonora of Tytalus then challenged him, sure he would not dare invite an outsider at the vaults; he put his marker there again, and she failed three times in the year. The primus was furious at his overconfidence, and a third use of the challenge was thought unlikely to go unpunished.

characters.name: Elonora of Tytalus
characters.summary: The maga who challenged the Archmage Velius after his filia failed, and made three failed attempts on the defenses of Coeris. She passed on what she remembered of them, and spread tales that Velius leaned on Hermanus' work rather than his own. From her stories magi tried to reckon the vis and seasons spent at Coeris, and the legend of its unbreachable defenses went through the Order, helped by the Tremere, who wished their sodales to think any raid futile.

characters.summary:
Thomae of Tytalus, c. 1122 to 1198, a showman and adventurer who made the boldest enchantment the Order has seen, a castle that flies, and a host of lesser magic items. He cared nothing for the wrangling his House loves. His challenge to himself was a boy's dream of living in a floating castle, and he paid for it by killing monsters and by hiring out to covenants at Wizard's War.

In 1191 he dropped from sight and came back with the castle. The alarm was great. After a tense tribunal he agreed to take it, high up and by night, to a range of mountains and stay there, where no mundane would see it and be provoked, and elder magi would not have to think of Wizard's War. He soon tired of that. By 1195 it was plain he was slipping out to sea in the dark and visiting desolate places in other Tribunals, and a tribunal met again; his politics saw him through, as no accuser could show that the Order had come to harm. In 1198, 22 years ago, he and the castle vanished. Some say he went to Transylvania to build weapons platforms for the Tremere, some that he is exploring, some that the Devil claimed him and the castle went to dust and ash in mid-air. Search has found nothing, and most magi expect some hint of him to surface.

Many want the castle and would pay well for it: the Hermetic Architects to study it for breakthroughs, the militant Houses as a weapons platform, supply engine or movable command post, House Mercere as a post for exchanging messages. His lesser items are rumored to carry folk between castle and ground, govern the weather and hurl gouts of fire. It is said they could defend the castle from any attack and let his whole turb fly, and his riches, taken from the far places of Europe and Africa, may be more folklore than fact.
characters.secrets:
His true end (p. 122): crossing the Alps, the castle overflew a griffon nesting site. With no Aegis, it could be attacked directly. A griffon clawed through the base of the High Tower to get at his treasury, and the castle listed and fell (the wreck's record has how). He wore an item that kept him from falling, so as the castle dropped he was dashed against the navigation room's ceiling. His remains are scattered through the wreck. He died by violence without rites, so his ghost can be reached and is probably deranged (p. 123), though the Faerie Dealings story supposes he left none (p. 138).

His great deceit (pp. 122-123): he gave out that a team of skilled helpers had made the castle by strange rituals and rare components, with mighty wards and weapons. In truth it is a bronze building on a lesser enchanted device made in one season, and his missing years were spent fitting out a laboratory big and secret enough for the Verditius he hired, and raising that magus's fee and silence. His life does not add up: too much is fitted in, and his notes show more ancillary items than he could have made or paid for (p. 138). See the stories of Thomae's Secret. How deep the deceit goes is the storyguide's.

What the Order Remembers (p. 122; roll Intelligence + Order of Hermes Lore, pp. 10-11; +3 for a character with some reason to care about his works or his legal case; the recollections may be false).

Ease Factor 0, Known to All:
- A magus of House Tytalus, active late last century.
- He built a flying castle.
- He had trouble at law.
- He vanished about 20 years ago.

Ease Factor 6, Widely Known:
- He vanished young for a magus, and many think he lives, tyrannizing natives somewhere remote in Africa or Asia.
- Politics bored him; flight was his obsession.
- His castle was of bronze.
- He was known as a slayer of magical beasts and a magical mercenary.
- He was charged with provoking mundanes by showing off his castle.
- He ranged far after vis to pay for it, long in the Holy Land and Africa.
- He settled his case by promising not to fly over civilized lands, though it was doubted he kept to it.

Ease Factor 12, Uncommon Knowledge:
- He told his tribunal that many of his magic items were bought, not made.
- The castle's costly safety gear for his servants won their loyalty.
- He claimed to be a Hermetic Architect, of one of the Order's least secret mystery societies.
- Quaesitores examined the castle during his case, but it was held to be his sanctum, so not even fellow Architects went aboard.

Ease Factor 18, Lost Secrets:
- His timeline is wrong: he seems to have fitted in more than he could, so he probably lied about what he did and when.
- He was probably no Hermetic Architect, though he said so.

Ease Factor 12, Hermetic Architects only:
- Many effects he called integral to the castle were impossible without a breakthrough in Hermetic Architecture.

characters.name: Andros
characters.summary: A former mercenary in his mid-twenties, now stealing unseen from the great houses of a large town. He keeps a bronze medal of Saint Thomas and thinks it holy.
characters.secrets:
No threat to a band of seasoned grogs. The book gives him no statistics: choose a generic to fit what he becomes after the story (p. 127). He got the medal from Roberto, whose vanishing in battle he saw, and made sure to take it when arrows killed Roberto. He thought of sending it home, but a tiny Alpine village seemed too much trouble. He has Roberto's other belongings, which may point to Santa Lucia, and knows where Roberto lies buried.

The medallion (pp. 127-128): small bronze on a chain of the same, a man's portrait on one side and a stylized castle on the other, like a pilgrim's medal. But Saint Thomas's marks are wrong (Intelligence + Church Lore 3): the halo is a spiral and nothing else names him, though Thomas is patron of architects, so the castle could pass. Maker's marks at the bottom edge. His garbled Latin prayer works because the triggers of two powers are 'Thomae' and the Latin for 'help'. It takes him two rounds, and he always uses both, not knowing they are separable. He knows the medal eases his landings, not that free fall does it. He does not know that blowing on it spies. Roberto did, which is why he kissed it before battle: to hear his commanders and get himself put in the reserve.

This one was made for training covenfolk: slower flight, far longer lasting. Scent of frying onions marks the maker's sigil while Aerial Dancer and Veil of Invisibility last.

Aerial Dancer: ReCo 35, Pen +0, unlimited/day. R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Individual. Spoken 'Thomae'. Moves the wearer through the air any way he likes at a running pace. Base 10, +1 Touch, +2 Sun; unlimited +10. The other medallions fly for two minutes at a running horse's speed (Base 15, +1 Touch, +1 Diameter; unlimited +10).
Failure to Fall: ReCo 25, Pen +0, unlimited/day. R: Touch, D: Diameter, T: Individual. Triggered by free fall. Lowers the faller about a foot a second for 120 feet, then reactivates if he is falling still, with a brief gap in the onion smell by which covenfolk claimed to judge their drop. Base 5, +1 Touch, +1 Diameter; unlimited +10. (The book says two minutes and, a sentence on, three.)
Veil of Invisibility: PeIm 25, Pen +0, 24 uses/day. R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Individual. Spoken 'help' in Latin. As the spell (ArM5 p. 146). Base 4, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 moving; 24 uses +5.
Whispering Winds: printed ReAu 15, Pen +0, 1 use/day. R: Sight, D: Concentration, T: Individual. Worked by blowing on the medallion. As the spell (ArM5 p. 127, which has it as InAu 15). Eavesdrops on a group in view. Unique.

Thomae's three shield grogs each had a medallion, a little different from each other, and his bodyguards made a strange three-dimensional martial art of them. The others are with the leaders of the Santa Lucians (p. 124).

characters.name: Roberto
characters.summary: A dead soldier of a mercenary company, who said he came from a tiny Alpine village called Santa Lucia and always kissed his medal before a fight.
characters.secrets: Son of Rogerio, whose medallion he stole before going off to soldier. Shot down by arrows. He died in battle and was buried anyhow, so his ghost can be summoned (p. 129). Returning his remains to Rogerio will be taken very kindly (p. 131).

characters.name: Rogerio
characters.summary: One of the three councilors of Santa Lucia, old now, who wears a metal badge of office.
characters.secrets: A ranking servant of Thomae, perhaps one of his guard. His badge replaces the medallion his son Roberto stole, and he wants the original back. He assumes at first that the characters took it from Roberto. His goodwill is worth having. He would not use a combat item now as he did when young, so another offer of position may sway him. Andros's story fits what he recalls of his reckless son (p. 131). The book gives no statistics.

characters.name: Flavia of Verditius
characters.summary: A living Verditius, maker of a bronze medal bearing a spiral. Her sigil is the smell of frying onions.
characters.secrets: She holds a fixed Arcane Connection to Thomae, taken to ensure he paid, and let him believe it destroyed. She has never used it, thinking he has made himself a king in Africa or Asia, and that it is folly to vex a magician-king with a flying fortress. The characters must persuade her with skill to let them use it. To go on to the search for the secret laboratory, the storyguide should send them by another lead (p. 129). The book does not say she is the castle's Verditius collaborator.

links.note: Made a medal for him; holds an Arcane Connection

creatures.name: The Magical Conciatta

params.circumstance: when not within a supernatural aura

abilities.name: Organization Lore: La Torre no Vista

powers.name: Crafter of Vim
powers.description: Focus Power: any Creo or Rego Vim effect of level 25 or less, at 1 Might point a magnitude. Init 0 minus the points spent.

powers.name: Eidolon
powers.description: Focus Power: an illusory form both seen and heard, made and unmade at will, and she always keeps it. Realms of Power: Magic p. 102.

powers.name: Ghost Touch
powers.description: Greater Power: moves objects not held or fastened down, 5 pounds for 1 Might point, doubling with each further point. In constant use, mostly beyond her control, and often drains her Might. Init 0 minus the points spent. Realms of Power: Magic p. 102.

powers.name: Master of Vim
powers.description: Focus Power: changes or destroys weak sources of magic she can perceive, as any Muto or Perdo Vim effect of level 25 or less, at 1 Might point a magnitude. Init 0 minus the points spent.

creatures.appearance: Two steps from presentable: her long hair is tied up and working loose, her fingers and once-fine gown are stained with ink. She works at a large orderly table in a storm of floating books, bottles and boxes, among flashes of light and glimpses of far places or old faces.
creatures.notes:
Scholar is her Essential Trait. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.

Might Form not printed. Things dart at intruders until she catches them, plainly with effort. She orders strangers out, then waits for proper overtures; in time she will find a reason to deal with them calmly (p. 25).
creatures.secrets: She knows she is dead and suspects a Final Twilight, prolonged and somehow made lasting, and that others like her may exist for the other realms. She knows she can learn nothing new of note, unless perhaps what follows if her Final Twilight is let finish (p. 25). Her books scrape over her own work again and again.

creatures.name: The Divine Conciatta

powers.name: Possession
powers.description: Focus Power: by spending all her Might she inhabits a target, her Personality Traits overlaying and adding to the host's. Thus she has held novices through the years.

powers.name: Grant (Visions)
powers.description: Ritual Power, used automatically on possession: gives the host the Visions Minor Story Flaw (ArM5 p. 60). Through it her memories of Hermetic work surface in the host.

powers.name: Grant (Enfeebled)
powers.description: Ritual Power x2, used automatically on possession: gives the host the Enfeebled Major Flaw (ArM5 p. 53).

creatures.appearance: She has no body, only a personality and a run of ill-fitting memories within her host. At the reunion she rises from the host as an angelic presence.
creatures.notes: The book prints no Characteristics or combat scores: she persists only within a host, the girl Immaculada. Her knowledge lies just below the surface of the mind, beyond conscious control: one who chooses to carry her has no conscious access to it, but bears her Personality Traits and gains the protection of her Divine Might. A new host suffers Enfeebled and Visions.
creatures.secrets: Visions in a new host may show her as a queen, wreathed in serpents, or in the heart of a great fire, or a shining city sinking under a mighty river (p. 32).

creatures.name: The Faerie Conciatta

abilities.name: Organization Lore: La Torre no Vista

powers.name: Grant (Insight of the Realms)
powers.description: Ritual; no Hermetic equivalent. Blesses the target with the Insight of the Realms Virtue for as long as she chooses. She regains the Might only by withdrawing the gift, and until then she in effect does not exist, reaching the world only by that withdrawal.

creatures.appearance: Young as she was in life, in a classical tunic and a cloak falling from her left shoulder, decked with silver and jewels. She sits beside the Silver King with her hand on his, and scorns all talk of the world she left.
creatures.notes: Her Abilities are Pretenses: she believes she is Conciatta, with deep knowledge of Hermetic Theory, and that she swore her magic away. She cannot be made to use her former powers, and being Incognizant cannot see the truth of what she is. Arganthonios imposes her Sovereign Ward; it lifts when his bargain is met. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.
creatures.secrets:
She is not truly Conciatta. The aspect the characters seek faded a century ago and became glamour, after pining for what she gave up and dying a second death; the true one had come back centuries ago to keep a bargain with the king. If reminded of her love for Currito she is released, and takes her role to be reunited with her sisters (pp. 38-39).

On leaving Tartessos her essence goes into the book Bruja gives: a quality 7 tractatus on Faerie Lore in somewhat archaic Hermetic Latin. The one given it gains one of her breakthroughs as a charm (Realms of Power: Faerie pp. 39, 104), usable while he carries the book and keeps it secret (p. 45).

creatures.name: The Infernal Conciatta

params.circumstance: when not within a supernatural aura

abilities.name: Organization Lore: La Torre no Vista

powers.name: Crafter of Vim
powers.description: Focus Power: any Creo or Rego Vim effect of level 25 or less, at 1 Might point a magnitude. Init 0 minus the points spent.

powers.name: Eidolon
powers.description: Focus Power: an illusory form both seen and heard, made and unmade at will, and she always keeps it. Realms of Power: Magic p. 102.

powers.name: Ghost Touch
powers.description: Greater Power: moves objects not held or fastened down, 5 pounds for 1 Might point, doubling with each further point. In constant use, mostly beyond her control, and often drains her Might. Init 0 minus the points spent. Realms of Power: Magic p. 102.

powers.name: Master of Vim
powers.description: Focus Power: changes or destroys weak sources of magic she can perceive, as any Muto or Perdo Vim effect of level 25 or less, at 1 Might point a magnitude. Init 0 minus the points spent.

powers.name: Hell's Onslaught
powers.description: Greater Power: as Pilum of Fire, +15 damage. Excess levels lower its cost, raise its initiative and master it, so she can loose two bolts together.

powers.name: Master of Stone
powers.description: Focus Power: any Muto or Perdo Terram effect of level 25 or less, at 1 Might point a magnitude. Init 0 minus the points spent.

creatures.appearance: Her skin glows as if fire boiled just beneath it, and her hair is drifting smoke. She is alluring, beautiful and all but naked.
creatures.notes:
Might Form not printed. The block repeats the Magic Spirit and the other Virtues of the Magical aspect. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.

Holy relics affect her, as she is a demon (p. 45). Her Qualities are as printed, though the block gives four powers marked Focus and two Greater.
creatures.secrets:
She mocks the visitors and says the Order's rules no longer bind her. If the host of the Divine aspect is there, she offers to let the others go for one life; she will not keep her word. Soon bored, she sends in her army. She watches for hastily drawn circles and breaks them with Master of Stone, and does not trust her penetration against Parma Magica (p. 44).

She will fight to the death. Her Might makes wards a hard way to bind her, and the troupe should be creative: holy relics; Perdo Vim to lower her Might; intense cold may harm her and force her to submit (pp. 44-45).

creatures.name: Seiffeddin the Actor
creatures.age: Appears to be in his late fifties

powers.name: Crafter of Illusion
powers.description: Focus Power: illusory props and sounds, as any Creo or Rego Imaginem effect of level 10 or less, at 1 Might point a magnitude. Never truly lifelike: they convey an idea or feeling. Init 0 minus the points spent.

powers.name: Eidolon
powers.description: Focus Power: an illusory form both seen and heard, made and unmade at will. Realms of Power: Magic p. 102.

powers.name: Master of Illusion
powers.description: Focus Power: alters the look of what he touches, as any Muto or Perdo Imaginem effect of level 10 or less, at 1 Might point a magnitude, always like stage props, scenery or costume. Init 0 minus the points spent.

creatures.equipment: A long white toga and various ephemeral props and masks.
creatures.appearance: An aging man with white hair and pale skin, dark dazzling eyes and a trained actor's mobile face. He moves with care, and his hands, like his expressions, are seldom still, marking every phrase. Illusions fill the theater around him with backcloth, scenery, props and sometimes other players.
creatures.notes: He contains no vis. His illusions spend his Might and leave him drained after each performance. Nervous of strangers, having been killed by one in life, he is welcoming once reassured. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.
creatures.secrets:
He remembers Conciatta and her quest for Tartessos. He taught her and Currito, with other spirits of Qadis, over a year, and under him they made a set of stones that added power to their magic; he offers the magi the same teaching. He can say how to reach Tartessos: only on the anniversary of its loss, a night the storyguide sets, and they must find Bruja out on the marsh (pp. 34-35).

The stones are ceremonial casting props (Houses of Hermes: Societates p. 59). A season of Magic Lore under him is a source of insight for Insight of the Realms, +10 to the initial roll. The maga must then enchant Clearing the Mind of the Caster, PeIm (Vi) 30, Pen +0, 1/day (R Touch, D Ring, T Circle): fifteen slate tablets, laced with leather and each carved with a symbol, laid around the caster in three rounds. Sensations not of the Magic realm are dulled as they cross in, though she may still attend to them; +1 to Concentration for activities wholly within, +3 as props in ceremonial casting. Re-creating it gives 6 points toward Insight of the Realms (p. 33).

creatures.name: Bruja, the Marsh Witch

powers.name: Spirit Away
powers.description: Greater Power: a brewed potion adds Threshold Points to a character's Threshold Total, 1 Might point each. The character must already have a Threshold Total, and she cannot supply all the points needed. Init is its magnitude divided by 2.

powers.name: The Malicious Brew
powers.description: Focus Power: brews any Perdo Corpus effect with an Individual target up to 9th magnitude into a poison, Might points equal to magnitude. It grows toward a set moment (sunset, full moon, cockcrow), giving time for a cure. Intelligence + Medicine simple roll against 9 tells how long the target has. She regains the Might when the effect ends.

powers.name: The Merciful Brew
powers.description: Lesser Power: a healing potion, as Purification of the Festering Wounds but with a Duration of Season, so it serves those recovering from heavy wounds. It instantly relieves a Malicious Brew. Might points equal to magnitude, regained when the effect ends.

creatures.appearance: A hunched crone, craggy and wrinkled, in a big-sleeved green cloak that trails behind her with plants growing in its threadbare weave. A satchel takes what she finds. She looks human until one sees her outsized lower legs, like a wading bird's, which carry her easily through the marsh.
creatures.notes:
The book prints her Abilities as Pretenses, and names Humanoid Form for what the catalog calls Humanoid Faerie. Her Virtues list Focus Power x2 though she has one Focus Power. Wound ranges: Light 1-5, Medium to 10, Heavy to 15, Incapacitated to 20, Dead from 21.

Her powers pass through potions, poultices, possets, bandages or whatever suits, often leeches or foul mixes of animal parts and marsh water. The Might goes at the brewing, and the potion waits until applied. Most are brewed with a given person in mind, so cause no Warping.
creatures.secrets: She will lead the characters to the gates if given a creature or herb not found in her marsh. She keeps no stock of potions, and brews each with spent Might; the Threshold draught is likely a live frog to be swallowed whole. Arganthonios can command her to give safe passage on a later visit (pp. 35-36, 39).

creatures.name: Arganthonios, the Silver King

powers.name: Binding Oath
powers.description: Ritual; no Hermetic equivalent. Enforces an oath freely sworn between two or more parties, penetrating the Magic Resistance of all. If one acts against it the others know at once. A human oath-breaker sees Arganthonios in every reflective surface; one who ignores that is struck blind, as the Flaw. That ends through powers that destroy mystical effects, by fulfilling the oath, by a new oath with the wronged faerie, or by destroying all the oath's other parties. Faeries cannot break oaths, though some roles seek loopholes.

creatures.equipment: A silver crown of laurel leaves, too large for a mortal head. A great spear with a silver shaft, an ivory head and a binding hung with peacock feathers.
creatures.appearance: A giant over eight feet tall, muscled like an oversized Greek statue, his body and beard of shining fluid silver and his brow heavy under his crown. He sits brooding on a raised dais in the ruined throne room, and when he speaks his voice is low, smooth and full of calm command.
creatures.notes: The crown is his External Vis, and gives its wearer Puissant Leadership and the Reclusive Flaw. He is Incognizant: for all his understanding he cannot change or better his role. The book spells them Pretences; Tartessos Lore is entered as an Area Lore. Wound ranges: Light 1-7, Medium to 14, Heavy to 21, Incapacitated to 28, Dead from 29.
creatures.secrets: Alone but for his queen, it is his nature to endure loss, and he frees her freely (p. 38). He made a bargain with Conciatta: she would rule beside him for knowledge of Faerie places, at the cost of renouncing her love for Currito. He explains what became of her, and offers that if the characters reunite this remnant with that love, he will release her to the world of men. If they cannot meet it yet, he gives them leave to go and return, and commands Bruja to grant safe passage (pp. 38-39).

creatures.name: Narixa Hyena

powers.name: Piercing the Infernal Veil
powers.description: Sees through the boundaries between regio levels. Improved Powers has brought its cost to 0 and raised its initiative.

creatures.appearance: Powerful shoulders, a sloping back and short rear legs make it look craven, but on the hunt it is nothing of the kind. It smiles at its prey's fear, and its eyes shine yellow in the dark.
creatures.notes: Ferocity applies against livestock. They roam the caves and leave them to hunt, more like wolves than natural hyena. A pack fights as a trained group: treat the Hyena trait as a score in Leadership. The book prints wounds of -1 (1-4), -3 (5-8), -5 (9-12), Incapacitated (13-16), Dead (21+); by those ranges Dead would be 17+.

creatures.name: Scorpion Swarm
creatures.appearance: A great shifting black sand of chitin and noise, covering everything in its path.
creatures.notes:
Venomous (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p. 43), at the level of an Asp's bite (ArM5 p. 180). The scent of magic maddens them, and they surge past defenders to reach magi (p. 44). The book prints wounds of -1 (1-6), -3 (7-12), -5 (13-18), Incapacitated (19-24), Dead (21+); by those ranges Dead would be 25+.

Optional swarm rules, for creatures of Size -3 or less totalling Size +1 or more: a swarm ignores defenders; it attacks as many targets each round as its Size; at the storyguide's discretion it may resist or ignore regular weapons; and unless destroyed outright it can disengage and come back at full strength after as many rounds as its highest wound penalty.

creatures.name: Tempestas

powers.name: Crafter of Weather
powers.description: Focus Power, 1-5 points: any non-Ritual weather effect up to level 25, at 1 Might per spell magnitude. A Slow Power, taking an extra round to prepare.

powers.name: Raise the Tempest
powers.description: CrAu 50 (base 5, +3 Sight, +1 Concentration, +2 Group, +3 Size), Greater Power, -5 Might from Improved Powers. A hurricane ten miles across, like Wrath of Whirling Winds and Water, which builds over several minutes and dies soon after the power ends.

creatures.appearance: To ordinary sight, only a great storm. Second Sight shows a huge disembodied blue head with bulging cheeks, ever blowing. The head is the size of a man; its Size does not count the storm.
creatures.notes:
Spirit of storms and the island's outer guard. When a ship or swimmer comes near it raises a storm that drives off or wrecks any vessel not protected by powerful magic, so those who expect a quiet anchorage are likely to land on the shore separately, with little gear (pp. 59-60).

Many of its weather effects are indirect, like capsizing a boat, but Tempest has Penetration 35, enough for direct effects such as lightning or rain to reach even magi.
creatures.secrets: Bound as guardian by Spell Binding in a carved agate head in the library (pp. 59-60). See the island's secrets for how the binding is built and broken.

creatures.name: Lucida

powers.name: Command Spirit
powers.description: ReMe 30 (base 5, +2 Voice, +3 Moon), Greater Power, -3 Might cost. If it penetrates, a disembodied spirit carries out her commands as best it can. It may try to break free when asked for anything complex, dangerous or against its nature: Intelligence + a fitting Personality Trait against Ease Factor 14 (9 + magnitude of her Might).

powers.name: Control Human
powers.description: ReMe 35 (base 20, +2 Voice, +1 Concentration), Greater Power, -3 Might cost. As Command Spirit, on a person, with the same chance to break free.

powers.name: Crafter of Illusion
powers.description: Focus Power, 1-5 points: any Creo or Rego Imaginem spell up to level 25, at 1 Might per magnitude.

powers.name: Greater Eidolon
powers.description: Cr(In)Im 30 (base 2, +3 Sight, +1 Concentration, +2 move at command, +1 intricacy, +1 Intellego requisite), Greater Power, -3 Might, +1 Init. An image she can see and hear through, anywhere she can see, moving and speaking as she directs even out of sight or after she Travels, until she has no more use for it: a youth in loose robes with short white hair and a high clear voice. In the villa it often appears inside a mirror.

powers.name: Ghost Touch
powers.description: Focus Power, 1-5 points: moves objects not held or fastened down, up to 5 pounds for 1 Might and double for each further point, until released. She cannot use or throw them as weapons.

powers.name: Travel
powers.description: ReMe 35 (base 15, +4 Special, as Arcane), Personal Power x2, -3 Might. Brings her to any place she can see, knows well or has an Arcane Connection to, much like a maga's ReCo travel spells.

creatures.appearance: No mortal form, and seldom in one place, her attention spread across the island. In her actual presence Second Sight shows a figure much like her image, a robed youth. She discourages speculation about what lies under the robes, though her name is feminine in Latin.
creatures.notes:
Chief spirit of the island, holding the others ready against the day her mistress returns. She still grieves, bound to the memory of the maga by her own will. Told of intruders, she turns the Imagines and the rest on them, to drive them mad or away (p. 67).

She calls herself an Airy Spirit, but she is far too strong for those minor spirits. Magic Lore scholars might call her a ghost, or a faerie who has moved into the Magic Realm.

A familiar's death note (p. 61): when a magus dies an ordinary animal familiar dies too, but immortal beings such as spirits are released and lose the Bond's powers.
creatures.secrets: Trapped by Cupressa and Monocaudus in the cleft of a huge boulder until Fortunata freed her and later came back to defeat and bind the beast. She may know what she really is and not be telling, or may truly have forgotten (p. 61). Only she knows the way into the laboratory (p. 62). She cannot force Monocaudus to obey; she can only repeat the old binding words and promise Fortunata's punishments, which feeds his hatred (p. 63).

creatures.name: Monocaudus

powers.name: Human Form
powers.description: He may, and is usually forced to, take human form for a Sun or until he ends it. It loses the serpent's Size +2, Str +4 and Qik -2, and has the Large Virtue, Size +1 with no change to his Characteristics. A Slow Power.

creatures.appearance: In truth a great serpent with the arms, chest and head of a man, his skin not scaled but covered in tattoos.
creatures.notes:
An ancient serpent and the household's resentful slave, kept to menial work and to human shape. He does the least he can, for fear she may yet come back, and curses her and Lucida to anyone who will listen, chiefly minor spirits who understand little of it.

Printed Virtues also include Size +2 (free), named here only. He was built by the rules for Dragons as Characters (Realms of Power: Magic p. 74). The block lists Personal Power (Human Form) twice; it is entered once.

Human form: Int 0, Per +1, Pre -1, Com +1, Str +2, Sta +3, Dex +2, Qik +2 (printed without a sign), Size +1. Wounds as a man: -1 (1-6), -3 (7-12), -5 (13-18), Incapacitated (19-24; printed 19-14). As a serpent: -1 (1-7), -3 (8-14), -5 (15-21), Incapacitated (22-28).

Human Form is an active power, so his man-form attacks must penetrate Magic Resistance. In his natural form they need not: a magus who has been shrugging off his fists may be surprised by the change. Constriction uses the grappling rules (ArM5 p. 174): while he holds a victim in his tail, the victim suffers Deprivation from lack of air, and he is free to strike or bite.

With her memory faded he may briefly defy his commands, rebelling or taking his true shape, on Stamina + a fitting Personality Trait against Ease Factor 12.
creatures.secrets:
Son of Cupressa and Omaion, and with his mother Lucida's tormentor. Fortunata and Lucida hunted and bound him, a Quest of her Initiation of Spirit Familiar (pp. 52, 57). Her summa calls him now human, now serpent, and the reading of his name is uncertain.

Monocaudus' Binding (p. 64): ReMe 55, Touch, Sun, Individual, Pen +32, constant (base 20, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +4 levels constant, +16 levels Penetration). A tiny enchanted topaz embedded in his chest, which renews the effect if it is ever suppressed. He must obey Fortunata, her continuing commands, or any agent she deputised. Guileful, he is very hard to convince of any new command's authority, even Lucida's. He talks himself out of his duties, and she had to chastise him even in her day. It may be possible, with difficulty, to pose as Fortunata well enough to rule him.

He does not know what binds him and blames Lucida (p. 64). He has never entered the laboratory (p. 62).

creatures.name: Fax

params.power: Arc of Fiery Ribbons, Continual Flame, Donning the Corporeal Veil, Hurl Flame
Arc of Fiery Ribbons, Continual Flame, Donning the Corporeal Veil, Hurl Flame

powers.name: Arc of Fiery Ribbons
powers.description: CrIg 25 (base 5, +2 Voice, +2 Group), Greater Power, -2 Might cost. As the spell: +10 damage to all in a 60-degree arc as far as her voice carries.

powers.name: Continual Flame
powers.description: CrIg 15 (base 3, +1 Touch, +3 Moon), Greater Power, -1 Might cost. Leaves a flame, candle- to torch-sized, on anything she touches, which burns a month with no fuel.

powers.name: Crafter of Ignem
powers.description: Focus Power, 1-3 points (15 levels, +1 add 5 to maximum level, +1 Init): any non-Ritual Creo or Rego Ignem spell up to level 15, at 1 Might per magnitude.

powers.name: Donning the Corporeal Veil
powers.description: Cr(Re)Ig 25 (base 5, +1 Touch, +2 Sun, +1 requisite), Greater Power, -1 Might cost. Makes and animates a body of elemental fire until the duration ends or she dissolves it. Slain in it she is killed, leaving 2 small rubies holding vis; injured, she can dissolve it to escape death.

powers.name: Flight of the Hummingbird
powers.description: ReIg 10, Personal Power, -1 Might cost. She flies in any direction by concentrating, and if that lapses she stops but does not fall. The block's reckoning says base 4, +2 Sun, against a printed Duration of Concentration.

powers.name: Hurl Flame

creatures.notes:
Spirit of the firebrand. By day she races about the island from bush tip to bush tip, never stopping to burn the wood; at night she may settle a while like a torch. She makes her fuelless flames when bored, and they last so long that many burn at any time in the interior and all through the villa. If commanded by Lucida, or if she remembers her charge, she harries and hurts intruders.

Fist of Flame burns on contact, not by impact. Wounds: -1 (1), -3 (2), -5 (3), Incapacitated (4). Her block also prints wound penalties under Powers; the errata deletes them (p. 78).

creatures.name: Cantus

powers.description: CrIm 25 (base 1, +2 Voice, +1 Concentration, +2 Group, +2 move at command, +1 intricacy), Greater Power, -3 Might, +2 Init. Music or simpler sounds, from one to ten voices. It favours bell chimes and plaintive melodies.

Filia of Gypaetus, who trained no apprentice and ended his line when she entered Final Twilight. A worker of air magics who built her sanctum high on a mountain. Her Inner Heartbeast is a Snowy Owl of Virtue, nesting on the tower roof.

She strikes from ambush: unseen and winning Initiative, +3 to her first Attack; still first in the order afterward, she can fly out of reach. To come round again, roll new Initiatives.

creatures.appearance: A pale, slightly see-through man in fourth-century BC armor, desperate and afraid, struggling with enemies who look just like him.
creatures.notes:
Combat figures apply only if it is made corporeal or uses Strike. Fights in trained groups of 4, group bonus +12. Veteran is printed among its Virtues; the catalog lacks it. Decrepitude n/a. Wounds: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

creatures.secrets: Vis: none in the spirit. When truly destroyed, not merely slain in the daily battle, 1 pawn of Mentem vis appears in the wreck of its ship, and the ship mends a little toward what it was before it sank.

creatures.name: Wooden Mannequin of Coeris
creatures.how_many: Six in the complex, two each in the store room, spare laboratory and sanctum; large supplies at Coeris
creatures.equipment: Chain hauberks in the store room, full chain in the spare laboratory; polearms with the House Tremere symbol on the head, crossbows and bolts.

creatures.notes: Figures printed for one animated by Ferox or Fidelius; another holder's Dexterity, Quickness and Abilities apply (Animate Mannequin). Soak n/a. Not hurt as living beings are, immune to pain and easily replaced; rules for limbs under the Staff of the Wooden Soldiers, in the Receiving Room's record.

powers.name: Ghostly Hands

powers.name: Ghostly Tongues

creatures.appearance: Unseen by most. Second Sight or fitting Intellego Vim shows a small sturdy statue of a man in a wizard's robes.
creatures.notes: A spirit of the element of Terram (Realms of Power: Magic p. 104), of one of the pair of granite statues in Hermanus' sanctum; Ferox and Fidelius share one printed block. Immaterial: they cannot manifest physically. No Soak, Fatigue or Wounds printed.
creatures.secrets:
Bound by old agreements with Hermanus to defend the complex, they know its defenses and devices well. Summoned by the Statue of Conjured Assistants, they go first to the receiving room for the Staves, then use the mannequins to carry justiciars and sentinels about against the intruders, keeping as far from magi as they can, perhaps slipping outside to act only through the dolls. If the mannequins of the spare laboratory are destroyed and they still hold the Staves, they will fetch Arcane Connections from the store room pair.

In the laboratory proper they find they can trigger the Butterfly's Gaze and the Tapestry of Confident Possession at will, and use them to fire any justiciar that helps. Once the ward against magical creatures is down they might, as a last resort, use the Helm of Unravelling, but are likelier to teach its use to any non-magus they think is under the Cross of the Preempted Conflict (errata p. 79).

They will not die for the laboratory. If destruction can be avoided only by flight or surrender they do that; if magi clearly mean to destroy them they leave and go overland to Coeris to warn the House. That takes a season, with finding it, drawing notice from outside its Aegis of the Hearth, and proving their good will. Entering the spare laboratory while the Hourglass or Prison stands there would trap them.

Faeries who settled into the dog-shaped finials on the castle's walls, and took their shape and manners from them. They hunt in packs, by nature and because their three powers together cost more than one dog's Might, and they fight as trained groups. Printed as Magic (Faerie?) Might: whether griffons are of Magic or Faerie is left open. The book prints no Communication ('Com -'). Grapple does no damage of its own, but on later rounds the griffon may add its Grapple Strength to the Attack Roll of its beak.

Spikes: joint spikes do +8 damage to anyone who lands a melee attack on it, grappling included. Brawl is 8 and +2 from Puissant, included in the printed figures. Fiercely territorial: only one should appear in any one scenario.

Wound ranges are as the block prints them. Light 1-8, Medium 9-16, Heavy 17-24 at -4 (the book prints -4 here, where the usual penalty is -5), Incapacitated 25-32, Dead from 33.

Horns come at adolescence, a straight pair from the forehead on most, with spikes from many joints, worst in the ruff, a ring of them guarding the throat and widest on the breast and between the shoulders; they are deadly to prey struggling in the griffon's grasp. Magi dispute what males are: the old texts do not mention them, though heraldry now and then does, and some suspect a faerie species living with the magical griffon, since they are found by nests they cannot fly to.

creatures.name: Mnemos
creatures.appearance: A dark-skinned man with a shaved head and a long waxed chin-beard, in a linen skirt and the ghost of a gold collar.
creatures.notes: An ancient ghost, dead since well before Christ, who recalls only a bright, hot sun and much sand. He speaks a tongue long forgotten, but could read in life and still can. He has no vis, and he has faded so far that he does not know why he stays on earth, and does not remember Fortunata.
creatures.secrets: One of the ghosts in The Names of Ghosts, where she annotated him 'Sumerian?'. She would call him, have him read scrolls aloud, and follow by Thoughts Within Babble, transcribing, or studying from his voice as from the text. The book prints no haunt for him.

creatures.name: Large Fish
creatures.appearance: A fish about the size of a person, 80 to 250 pounds.
creatures.notes: The form given by Cloak of Fins and Scales. Defense +4 with Teeth and +5 with Dodge against grapples. Confidence 0; a group under attack gains the Ferocity Virtue, so Confidence 1 (3), but one attacked alone does not. Wounds: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20), Dead (21+).

creatures.name: Large Shark
creatures.appearance: A shark of Size +2.
creatures.notes: The form given by Form of the Aquatic Predator. Ferocity lets it spend Confidence only when attacking prey (Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p. 40). Wounds: -1 (1-7), -3 (8-14), -5 (15-21), Incapacitated (22-28), Dead (29+).

creatures.name: Elemental Blizzard

params.detail: Chill Touch cost -2, Charge of the Angry Winds cost -1 and Init +2, Drown Init +5

powers.name: Chill Touch
powers.description: Its freezing touch does +10 damage, and metal armor gives no benefit against it.

powers.name: Charge of the Angry Winds
powers.description: As the spell of that name, adding the elemental's Strength to every Ease Factor for acting within the wind.

powers.name: Drown
powers.description: It wraps a victim and fills her lungs with ice, forcing a Deprivation roll (ArM5 pp. 180-181). She may break free by the Grappling rules (ArM5 p. 174).

creatures.appearance: A menacing grey fog with shapes of men and animals in it.
creatures.notes:
An encounter for parties on the way to the crash site, built as a water elemental by Realms of Power: Magic. It has no self to speak of: it attacks because it is a blizzard's rage, not from hatred or to guard anything. It may attack up to its Size in enemies a round. Its immunity to fire and its disregard for much armor make it hard on groups weak in combat magic.

Injured, it loses Might equal to the wound's penalty. Large pieces broken off in combat hold part of its vis; it always knows where they are and tries to rejoin them. Wound ranges: Light 1-8, Medium to 16, Heavy to 24, Incapacitated to 32, Dead from 33. As printed.

creatures.name: Despair Demon

powers.name: Coagulation
powers.description: Gives it a body, a spiked ball of icicles a yard wide. Forming takes a round; it can shed the body almost at once.

powers.name: Elemental Control of Air
powers.description: Any Creo, Muto or Rego Auram effect at 1 Might a magnitude (variable cost), minor effects only, of level no more than its Might Score. It hides paths, wipes footprints, cuts visibility and smothers cries for help to part stragglers from a group.

powers.name: Envisioning
powers.description: Small changes to a victim's dreams, making them darker and more ominous.

powers.name: Obsession
powers.description: When a human commits a venial sin and the demon spends Might in reply, it may force spiritual doubt. At the next crisis of worthiness the storyguide rolls a simple die +3, the player a simple die + a suitable Personality Trait, with adjustments for a harsh environment. If the demon's total is higher the character gains Doubt +1. Acting on that score puts him in a state of sin, and the demon coagulates and kills him.

creatures.appearance: A ball of icicles a yard across.
creatures.notes: These prey on travelers in the Alps, confusing and separating them. Worn by privation and the fear of death, a victim may lose faith in the Lord, and the demon then kills him before he can repent. Best used on those who leave the group, like scouts or foragers. Built by Realms of Power: The Infernal. The book prints no Art for its vis. Wound ranges: Light 1-6, Medium to 12, Heavy to 18, Incapacitated to 24, Dead from 25. As printed.

source: Legends of Hermes, by Atlas Games; summarised, not quoted.
